> **Repository/privacy note**
>
> This repository should contain code and documentation only. Raw survey data,
> linkage files, editable audit files, receipts, processed participant-level
> outputs, and rendered HTML are intentionally kept outside version control.
> Some generated audit files contain direct identifiers (including names and
> Qualtrics ResponseIds) and must remain in approved secure project storage.
>
> The script is designed as a staged workflow. When a new editable audit file is
> created, execution stops so that the file can be reviewed manually before the
> corresponding decisions are applied on the next run.


GUTS WP2 Behavioral Cleaning Pipeline (Wave-Specific)
Purpose

This document provides a complete, wave specific behavioral data cleaning pipeline for the GUTS WP2 project. The goal is to take raw Qualtrics exports (SPSS .sav files) and transform them into clean, well documented, and shareable datasets that are consistent across waves.

The pipeline is designed to be readable, auditable, and reproducible. Every major cleaning decision is recorded in human editable audit files, allowing manual verification without requiring the user to directly modify code.



Overview of the Pipeline

The cleaning workflow is organized into three major phases.



Phase 1: Identity Resolution and PPN Repair

The early steps focus on stabilizing participant identifiers (PPNs). In this project, the primary identifier originates in the Informed Consent file, where the Qualtrics ResponseId functions as the canonical PPN that should propagate across all downstream survey parts.

Key tasks in this phase include:

Detecting and removing test or researcher responses

Recovering missing PPNs in downstream survey parts

Resolving cases where the same PPN was shared across multiple participants

Resolving IC restarters (same person submitting IC multiple times with different ResponseId values)



Phase 2: Linking Participants to GUTS Subject IDs

After PPNs have been stabilized, participant identities are linked to the master linkage file (Name ↔ gutsID). Once a gutsID is assigned, it is propagated to all downstream datasets (Part 1, Part 2, Sensitive Data, and Financial Compensation).

This step produces a consistent identifier structure that supports:

Longitudinal merging across waves

Anonymized analysis workflows

Clean sociometric mapping



Phase 3: Survey Content Cleaning and Export Preparation

After identity and gutsID linkage are complete, additional cleaning steps are applied to survey specific content. A major example is sociometric data cleaning, where variable labels may contain identifiable nominee names and must be mapped to gutsID values.



Audit Structure (Write → Edit → Read → Apply)

Most cleaning steps follow the same audit pattern:

Write: Export a self contained audit CSV describing potential issues

Edit: The user manually edits decision columns in the CSV

Read: The script re imports the edited audit file

Apply: The script applies only explicitly approved fixes

This approach minimizes silent cleaning decisions and creates a transparent record of what was changed and why.




Outputs

The pipeline generates three main classes of outputs.

Audit Files (editable decision files)

These are the primary user facing outputs during cleaning. Each audit step produces a single review file that contains evidence columns and decision columns.


Receipts (applied change summaries)

Some steps optionally write receipts showing only the changes that were applied. These are stored separately from the main audit review files.


Reports (read only participation and identity summaries)

A full identity ledger is exported as a read only report. This ledger is useful for tracking participation patterns and determining which subjects represent true respondents versus incomplete or invalid entries.



Final Export

Load an external Qualtrics measure overview file

Use that overview to define which variables belong to each measure

Split the cleaned survey datasets into measure level exports

Export each measure as a standalone sharable dataset

Enforce GUTS naming conventions for all exported files

Generate standardized metadata files accompanying each export

The end result will be a complete wave specific export package containing cleaned, well labeled datasets for every individual measure collected during the wave.




Expected Inputs

This pipeline assumes the following wave specific raw inputs exist:

Informed Consent (IC) SPSS export(s)

Survey Part 1 SPSS export

Survey Part 2 SPSS export

Sensitive Data SPSS export

Financial Compensation SPSS export

Master linkage file (Excel), mapping Name ↔ gutsID



Expected Final Objects (in memory)

By the end of identity cleaning and linkage, the main cleaned objects will be:

ic_ledger_final

part1_final

part2_final

sensitive_final

financial_final

Each of these will contain a valid gutsID column and a stabilized identifier structure that supports downstream analysis and wave to wave harmonization.


```{r}
###############################################################################
#Libraries and data import
###############################################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(haven)
  library(dplyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(stringi)
  library(tibble)
  library(readxl)
})

# ---- repository-safe configuration ----
# Keep the private data root outside the Git repository.
# Example (Windows, set in ~/.Renviron):
#   GUTS_DATA_ROOT=X:/secure/project/data
dir0 <- Sys.getenv("GUTS_DATA_ROOT", unset = "")
if (!nzchar(dir0)) {
  stop(
    "GUTS_DATA_ROOT is not set. Point it to the private GUTS data root ",
    "before running this pipeline."
  )
}
dir0 <- normalizePath(dir0, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

# Optional private configuration for participant/researcher-specific patches.
# Keep this file outside the repository. It may define objects such as:
#   researcher_names
#   sociometric_name_patches
private_config <- Sys.getenv("GUTS_PRIVATE_CONFIG", unset = "")
if (nzchar(private_config)) {
  if (!file.exists(private_config)) {
    stop("GUTS_PRIVATE_CONFIG does not exist: ", private_config)
  }
  source(private_config, local = TRUE)
}

# Avoid embedding participant-level console output in rendered HTML.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  results = "hide",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

# ---- raw file paths (Wave-specific) ----
paths <- list(
  ic_main = file.path(dir0, "Behavioral/T1/data_raw/GUTS+WP2+T1+Informed+Consent_January+15,+2026_04.21.sav"),
  ic_fu   = file.path(dir0, "Behavioral/T1/data_raw/GUTS+WP2+T1+Informed+Consent+(Follow-up)_January+21,+2026_03.10.sav"),
  part1   = file.path(dir0, "Behavioral/T1/data_raw/GUTS+WP2+T1+-+part+1_January+15,+2026_03.56.sav"),
  part2   = file.path(dir0, "Behavioral/T1/data_raw/GUTS+WP2+T1+-+part+2_January+15,+2026_04.20.sav"),
  sensitive = file.path(dir0, "Behavioral/T1/data_raw/GUTS+WP2+T1+Sensitive+Data_January+21,+2026_03.10.sav"),
  financial_comp = file.path(dir0, "Behavioral/T1/data_raw/GUTS+WP2+T1+Financial+Compensation_January+21,+2026_03.12.sav")
)

read_sav_tagged <- function(path, label) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(path))
  df <- read_sav(path) %>% as_tibble()
  message(label, ": ", nrow(df), " rows, ", ncol(df), " cols")
  df
}

# ---- read everything ----
ic_main <- read_sav_tagged(paths$ic_main, "ic_main")
ic_fu   <- read_sav_tagged(paths$ic_fu, "ic_fu")
part1   <- read_sav_tagged(paths$part1, "part1")
part2   <- read_sav_tagged(paths$part2, "part2")
sensitive <- read_sav_tagged(paths$sensitive, "sensitive")
financial_comp <- read_sav_tagged(paths$financial_comp, "financial_comp")

file_linkage <- file.path(dir0, "T1_Behavioral/Hackathon/GUTS_WP2_Linkage.xlsx")
linkage <- read_excel(file_linkage)
```


```{r}
###############################################################################
#Helper functions: names and dates
###############################################################################
# These helpers standardize names and timestamps so comparisons behave
# consistently across SPSS imports and Qualtrics exports.
#
# clean_name():
#   - produces a lowercase, whitespace-squished, NFC-normalized string
#   - used as the stable matching key for identity operations
#
# fix_tussenvoegsels():
#   - normalizes common Dutch tussenvoegsels after title-casing
#   - improves linkage later when matching to the master linkage file
#     containing GUTS subject IDs (where naming conventions are typically
#     “Title Case + correct tussenvoegsels”)
#
# parse_dt_any():
#   - parses both timestamp formats observed across files
#   - returns POSIXct in UTC for consistent wave-wide comparisons
###############################################################################

clean_name <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_squish() %>%
    str_to_lower() %>%
    stringi::stri_trans_nfc()
}

fix_tussenvoegsels <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sVan\\s", " van ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sDer\\s", " der ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sDe\\s",  " de ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sDen\\s", " den ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sTer\\s", " ter ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sLe\\s",  " le ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\sTot\\s", " tot ")
}

parse_dt_any <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  out1 <- suppressWarnings(as.POSIXct(x, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))
  out2 <- suppressWarnings(as.POSIXct(x, format = "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))
  ifelse(!is.na(out1), out1, out2) %>% as.POSIXct(tz = "UTC", origin = "1970-01-01")
}
```


Audit Framework Overview (Write → Edit → Read → Apply)

A central goal of this pipeline is to ensure that all major cleaning decisions are transparent, reproducible, and manually verifiable. Rather than applying automatic fixes silently, the script uses an audit based workflow in which each major cleaning step produces a single editable audit file that documents the evidence for a potential issue and allows the user to decide how the issue should be handled.

This framework is designed so that a new user can run the script, review a small number of clearly structured audit files, and apply decisions without needing to rewrite the underlying code.



General Workflow Used in Every Audit Step

Each audit step follows the same sequence:

Write
The script generates a self contained audit CSV file that includes:

the rows or cases requiring review

relevant context and evidence columns to support decision making

editable decision columns (for example keep, apply_fix, or ppn_new)



Edit
The user manually edits the audit file using Excel or another spreadsheet editor.
Only the clearly labeled decision columns should be edited. Evidence columns should be treated as read only.



Read
The script re imports the edited audit file and performs safety checks to ensure that:

rows were not deleted

rows were not reordered

key identifiers match the originally exported file



Apply
The script applies the user’s decisions to the dataset and produces updated working objects that will be used in all later steps.



This approach ensures that every meaningful decision is explicitly documented and traceable.




Why This Structure is Necessary

Qualtrics based datasets often contain irregularities that cannot be safely corrected using purely automated rules. Common issues include test responses, survey restarts, missing participant identifiers, shared survey links, and ambiguous identity collisions. In many cases the correct resolution requires human judgment.

The audit framework makes these issues manageable by forcing them into small, structured decision points, while keeping the rest of the pipeline fully reproducible.



Audit Step Philosophy

Each audit step is designed to handle a single class of data quality issue. The steps are intentionally ordered so that earlier fixes prevent later steps from surfacing unnecessary noise. For example, removing test participants early prevents them from contaminating later identity resolution steps.

By the end of the audit sequence, the datasets should contain stable identifiers that can be reliably linked to gutsID and used for downstream analysis and data sharing.



Typical Outputs from Each Audit Step

Each audit step produces one primary review file that serves as the authoritative record of decisions for that step. Some steps may also generate optional receipts or read only reports for tracking and documentation purposes.

The primary audit files should be preserved in approved secure project storage because they serve as the complete record of manual decisions made during cleaning. They may contain direct identifiers and should not be committed to a public repository.



```{r}
###############################################################################
#Audit IO helpers (WRITE -> EDIT -> READ -> APPLY)
###############################################################################
# Each audit step writes a small CSV to audit_dir. You edit it once,
# re-import it, and we apply the decisions before the next step.
###############################################################################

audit_dir <- file.path(dir0, "Behavioral", "T1", "audit_outputs")
if (!dir.exists(audit_dir)) dir.create(audit_dir, recursive = TRUE)

write_audit_csv <- function(df, filename) {
  out_path <- file.path(audit_dir, filename)
  write.csv2(df, file = out_path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
  message("Wrote audit file: ", out_path)
  invisible(out_path)
}

read_audit_csv2 <- function(filename) {
  in_path <- file.path(audit_dir, filename)
  stopifnot(file.exists(in_path))
  read.csv2(in_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Editable audit files are deliberately different from read-only reports.
# On first creation, stop execution if there are rows to review. On later runs,
# preserve the edited file rather than overwriting the reviewer's decisions.
write_review_csv <- function(df, filename) {
  out_path <- file.path(audit_dir, filename)

  if (file.exists(out_path)) {
    message("Using existing review file: ", out_path)
    return(invisible(out_path))
  }

  write.csv2(df, file = out_path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
  message("Wrote review file: ", out_path)

  if (nrow(df) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Manual review required. Edit the decision columns in ", filename,
      " in secure project storage, then re-run this audit step."
    )
  }

  invisible(out_path)
}
```



Audit Step A: Identifying and Removing Test Responses

The first audit step focuses on detecting and removing test or researcher generated survey entries. These responses are common in Qualtrics datasets because researchers often access the survey multiple times during development, piloting, or troubleshooting. If these rows are not removed early, they can contaminate downstream cleaning steps by introducing false participant identities and invalid PPNs.

This step is intentionally placed at the very beginning of the pipeline because the Informed Consent (IC) dataset defines the participant identifier system used throughout the entire project. In this pipeline, the Qualtrics ResponseId from IC is treated as the canonical participant identifier (PPN). Once a test ResponseId is removed from IC, that identifier is also removed globally from all downstream survey parts to ensure consistency.



How Test Responses Are Flagged

Potential test responses are flagged using two conservative criteria:

Pre-launch timestamps: IC entries submitted before the official wave launch time are highly likely to represent pilot or development activity.

Researcher name matching: IC entries where the participant name matches a known researcher name list, or explicitly contains the word "test", are also flagged.

These criteria are used only to generate a candidate list. No rows are automatically removed without review.




Manual Review and Decision Process

This step exports a single audit file containing only the IC rows that were flagged as potential tests. The file includes the relevant evidence needed to make decisions, such as timestamps, the flag source, and the reason for flagging.

The user then reviews the file and specifies whether each flagged response should be kept or dropped.



Output of Step A

After the edited audit file is re imported, all IC ResponseId values marked for removal are treated as invalid PPNs. These identifiers are removed from:

Informed Consent (IC)

Part 1

Part 2

Sensitive Data

Financial Compensation

Additionally, the Financial Compensation dataset is also filtered by participant name to remove cases where test names appear even if the PPN field is missing or unreliable.

By the end of Step A, all downstream cleaning steps operate on a dataset that is substantially cleaner and less contaminated by non participant entries.


```{r}
###############################################################################
# Audit Step A: Identify and remove test responses (IC is the source of truth)
#
# Goal
# This audit step removes researcher and test activity as early as possible.
# In this pipeline, the Informed Consent (IC) file defines the participant
# identifier system for the entire wave. Specifically, the Qualtrics ResponseId
# in IC is treated as the canonical participant identifier (PPN) that should
# propagate downstream into Part 1, Part 2, Sensitive Data, and Financial
# Compensation.
#
# Strategy
# Audit Step A has four stages:
#   A1. Construct the full IC universe for the wave (IC main + IC follow up)
#       and compute conservative test flags.
#   A2. Write one self contained review file for flagged IC ResponseIds.
#   A3. Re import the edited review file and drop ResponseIds marked as tests.
#   A4. Propagate the test drops globally by removing those PPNs from all
#       downstream datasets (and remove matching test names from Financial).
#
# Outputs
#   - A_test_drop_decisions.csv   (EDIT THIS FILE)
#
# Notes on object naming
# We keep an object called ic_ledger_raw for historical reasons, but after
# Audit Step A is applied, ic_ledger_raw is overwritten to contain the working
# (post test drop) IC ledger. This is intentional to keep later steps clean,
# but it means ic_ledger_raw is no longer truly raw after this point.
###############################################################################


###############################################################################
# A1. Build the IC universe and compute conservative test flags (flag only)
###############################################################################

# ---- WAVE SPECIFIC: official launch time ----
# IC entries before this time are strong candidates for piloting or testing.
real_start <- as.POSIXct("2024-11-11 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")

# ---- WAVE SPECIFIC: researcher and test names ----
# Practical guidance: open the raw IC SPSS file and sort by StartDate to
# identify the earliest entries. Those are often researcher tests.
if (!exists("researcher_names", inherits = FALSE)) {
  researcher_names <- character(0)
}

# Clean researcher names once so matching is deterministic
researcher_names_clean <- clean_name(researcher_names)

# Combine IC files and standardize key fields
ic_combined <- bind_rows(ic_main, ic_fu) %>%
  rename(Name = ic_name) %>%
  mutate(
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate),
    ResponseId      = as.character(ResponseId),
    ppn             = as.character(ppn),
    Name_title      = fix_tussenvoegsels(str_to_title(as.character(Name))),
    Name_clean      = clean_name(Name_title),

    # Flag only: we decide what to drop in the audit CSV
    flag_test_by_date = !is.na(StartDate_posix) & StartDate_posix < real_start,

    # Exact match only: direct list match or literal "test" in the name
    flag_test_by_name = ifelse(
      is.na(Name_clean) | Name_clean == "",
      FALSE,
      (Name_clean %in% researcher_names_clean) | str_detect(Name_clean, "\\btest\\b")
    )
  )

# IC ledger for auditing: full IC universe with flags but no decisions applied
ic_ledger_raw <- ic_combined %>%
  select(
    Name, Name_title, Name_clean,
    ResponseId, ppn,
    StartDate, EndDate, StartDate_posix, EndDate_posix,
    flag_test_by_date, flag_test_by_name
  )


###############################################################################
# A2. WRITE: export one review file for flagged IC ResponseIds (edit decisions)
###############################################################################
# This file is intentionally self contained so a reviewer can decide whether
# each flagged ResponseId should be kept or dropped without needing to inspect
# other objects.
#
# Editable fields
#   - keep
#   - drop_reason
#   - notes
#
# Do not edit
#   - ResponseId
#   - Name_clean
###############################################################################

test_rows_review <- ic_ledger_raw %>%
  mutate(
    flag_test = flag_test_by_date | flag_test_by_name,
    test_reason = case_when(
      flag_test_by_date & flag_test_by_name ~ "prelaunch + researcher_name_or_test",
      flag_test_by_date ~ "prelaunch",
      flag_test_by_name ~ "researcher_name_or_test",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(flag_test) %>%
  arrange(StartDate_posix) %>%
  select(
    Name, Name_title, Name_clean,
    ResponseId, ppn,
    StartDate_posix, EndDate_posix,
    flag_test_by_date, flag_test_by_name, test_reason
  )

test_drop_decisions_template <- test_rows_review %>%
  transmute(
    # identity keys (do not edit)
    ResponseId,
    Name_title,
    Name_clean,

    # audit context
    StartDate_posix,
    EndDate_posix,
    flag_test_by_date,
    flag_test_by_name,
    test_reason,

    # editable decisions
    keep = FALSE,
    drop_reason = test_reason,
    notes = ""
  )

write_review_csv(test_drop_decisions_template, "A_test_drop_decisions.csv")


###############################################################################
# A3. READ + APPLY: re import the edited decisions and drop marked tests
###############################################################################

test_drop_decisions <- read_audit_csv2("A_test_drop_decisions.csv")

# Guardrails: do not allow deletions or reordering
stopifnot(all(test_drop_decisions$ResponseId %in% test_drop_decisions_template$ResponseId))
stopifnot(all(test_drop_decisions$ResponseId == test_drop_decisions_template$ResponseId))

drop_test_responseids <- test_drop_decisions %>%
  filter(keep == FALSE) %>%
  pull(ResponseId) %>%
  unique()

# Apply drops to IC (create post Step A working IC objects)
ic_combined_working <- ic_combined %>%
  filter(!(ResponseId %in% drop_test_responseids))

ic_ledger_working <- ic_ledger_raw %>%
  filter(!(ResponseId %in% drop_test_responseids))


###############################################################################
# A4. APPLY GLOBALLY: remove dropped test PPNs from downstream datasets
###############################################################################
# After Audit Step A, any IC ResponseId marked for removal is treated as an
# invalid PPN for the wave. Because IC ResponseId is the identifier that
# propagates downstream, we drop these PPNs from Part 1, Part 2, Sensitive,
# and Financial.
#
# Financial contains both PPNs and names. To handle cases where the PPN is
# missing or unreliable, we also drop financial rows whose cleaned name
# matches a dropped test name.
#
# Implementation note
# We overwrite ic_combined and ic_ledger_raw to keep later audit tables clean.
# From this point onward, ic_ledger_raw refers to the post Step A working IC.
###############################################################################

test_name_clean_drop <- test_drop_decisions %>%
  filter(keep == FALSE) %>%
  pull(Name_clean) %>%
  unique()

# 1) IC: overwrite the main objects used downstream in the script
ic_combined <- ic_combined_working
ic_ledger_raw <- ic_ledger_working

# 2) Downstream datasets: drop by PPN where available
part1 <- part1 %>%
  mutate(ppn = as.character(ppn)) %>%
  filter(!(ppn %in% drop_test_responseids))

part2 <- part2 %>%
  mutate(ppn = as.character(ppn)) %>%
  filter(!(ppn %in% drop_test_responseids))

sensitive <- sensitive %>%
  mutate(ppn = as.character(ppn)) %>%
  filter(!(ppn %in% drop_test_responseids))

# 3) Financial: drop by PPN and also by name (best effort)
financial_comp <- financial_comp %>%
  mutate(
    ppn = as.character(ppn),
    fc_name = as.character(fc_name),
    fc_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(str_to_title(fc_name)),
    fc_name_clean = clean_name(fc_name_title)
  ) %>%
  filter(!(ppn %in% drop_test_responseids)) %>%
  filter(!(fc_name_clean %in% test_name_clean_drop))


###############################################################################
# Post Step A standardization: add parsed timestamps to downstream datasets
###############################################################################
# This is not a new audit step. It prepares Part 1, Part 2, Sensitive, and
# Financial for later audit steps that use time matching or completion checks.
###############################################################################

part1 <- part1 %>%
  mutate(
    ppn = as.character(ppn),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

part2 <- part2 %>%
  mutate(
    ppn = as.character(ppn),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

sensitive <- sensitive %>%
  mutate(
    ppn = as.character(ppn),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

financial_comp <- financial_comp %>%
  mutate(
    ppn = as.character(ppn),
    fc_name = as.character(fc_name),
    fc_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(str_to_title(fc_name)),
    fc_name_clean = clean_name(fc_name_title),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

```


Audit Step B: Recover Missing PPNs Using a Backward, Anchor Based Strategy

This audit step repairs missing participant identifiers (ppn) in the main survey components. In this project, ppn is the key that links each participant’s survey responses across files, and missing values can break all downstream joins and identity resolution.



Why Financial Is the Anchor

The survey flow for each wave is:

IC → Sensitive → Part 1 → Part 2 → Financial

When ppn goes missing, it often disappears not just in one file, but in that file and any subsequent files in the sequence. Critically, Financial is the only downstream file that contains a participant name field that can reliably map back to IC, which is where the canonical participant identifier lives (IC ResponseId, which functions as the wave’s canonical ppn). For that reason, Financial must serve as the final anchor for recovering missing PPNs.



High Level Strategy

Step B uses a backward solving approach that starts closest to the anchor and works upstream only when needed:

Preflight check for missing ppn values
We first scan the main downstream survey components: Sensitive, Part 1, and Part 2 (excluding IC).
This step is purely diagnostic and determines whether any recovery work is required.



Recover missing PPNs only where necessary, in a backward order

Part 2 first: recover missing ppn by time matching Part 2 to Financial, then using the matched Financial name to map back to IC and retrieve the canonical ppn.

Part 1 next (only if needed): recover missing ppn by time matching Part 1 to Part 2 (which should now be repaired), then continuing the chain from Part 2 to Financial to IC to retrieve the canonical ppn.

Sensitive last (only if needed): recover missing ppn by time matching Sensitive to Part 1 (which should now be repaired), then continuing the chain forward through Part 1 and Part 2 to Financial and back to IC.



Single manual review file, conservative application
All proposed repairs are written to a single review file that includes the evidence used at each link in the chain (timestamps, candidate matches, names, and recovered ppn). The script applies fixes only when explicitly approved in the review file.



Output of Step B

Step B produces:

One review file (editable): B_missing_ppn_review.csv
This file contains all candidates requiring review, across any survey components that actually have missing PPNs in the current wave.

Optional receipts (recommended for traceability): compact summaries of what was changed, written separately from the main review file.

By the end of Step B, all survey components have a maximally complete ppn column, enabling reliable identity resolution and linkage in subsequent steps.


```{r}
###############################################################################
# AUDIT STEP B: missing ppn in main survey chain (Part 2 -> Part 1 -> Sensitive)
#   Output: ONE review file + receipts written to receipts/ subfolder
###############################################################################
# Prereqs expected in environment (from earlier sections):
#   - audit_dir, write_audit_csv(), read_audit_csv2()
#   - parse_dt_any(), clean_name(), fix_tussenvoegsels()
#   - ic_combined (or ic_combined_working after Step A test drops)
#   - part2, part1, sensitive, financial_comp
###############################################################################

# -------------------------
# 0) Parameters + folders
# -------------------------
tolerance_secs <- 2

receipts_dir <- file.path(audit_dir, "receipts")
if (!dir.exists(receipts_dir)) dir.create(receipts_dir, recursive = TRUE)

write_receipt_csv <- function(df, filename) {
  out_path <- file.path(receipts_dir, filename)
  write.csv2(df, file = out_path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
  message("Wrote receipt file: ", out_path)
  invisible(out_path)
}

# -------------------------
# 1) Local helpers (self-contained for this section)
# -------------------------
is_missing_ppn <- function(x) {
  x2 <- trimws(as.character(x))
  is.na(x2) |
    x2 == "" |
    x2 %in% c("NA", "N/A", "NULL") |
    grepl("^\\{e://Field/.*\\}$", x2)
}

has_missing_ppn <- function(df, col = "ppn") {
  if (!col %in% names(df)) return(FALSE)
  any(is_missing_ppn(df[[col]]))
}

normalize_progress <- function(x) {
  out <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  out[is.na(out)] <- -Inf
  out
}

normalize_finished <- function(x) {
  x_chr <- trimws(tolower(as.character(x)))
  dplyr::case_when(
    x_chr %in% c("1", "true", "t", "yes", "y") ~ 1,
    x_chr %in% c("0", "false", "f", "no", "n") ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ -Inf
  )
}

safe_nonmissing_count <- function(df) {
  rowSums(!is.na(df) & trimws(as.character(df)) != "")
}

# Strict time match helper:
# Returns best match index + diagnostics, or NA if nothing within tolerance.
time_match_one <- function(target_time, candidate_times, tolerance_secs) {
  if (is.na(target_time) || length(candidate_times) == 0) {
    return(list(best_index = NA_integer_, best_abs_diff = NA_real_, n_within_tol = 0L))
  }
  diffs_abs <- abs(as.numeric(difftime(candidate_times, target_time, units = "secs")))
  n_within <- sum(diffs_abs <= tolerance_secs, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (all(is.na(diffs_abs))) {
    return(list(best_index = NA_integer_, best_abs_diff = NA_real_, n_within_tol = as.integer(n_within)))
  }
  best_idx <- which.min(diffs_abs)
  best_abs <- diffs_abs[best_idx]
  if (is.na(best_abs) || best_abs > tolerance_secs) {
    return(list(best_index = NA_integer_, best_abs_diff = best_abs, n_within_tol = as.integer(n_within)))
  }
  list(best_index = as.integer(best_idx), best_abs_diff = as.numeric(best_abs), n_within_tol = as.integer(n_within))
}

# Resolve collisions introduced by Step B repairs in Part 2 only.
# This is intentionally narrow:
#   - only rows explicitly repaired in Step B are considered
#   - only ppns touched by those repairs are checked
#   - only duplicated ppns among those touched values are resolved
resolve_part2_postrepair_collisions <- function(part2_df, repaired_row_ids) {

  if (length(repaired_row_ids) == 0) {
    empty_review <- tibble::tibble(
      ppn = character(),
      row_id = integer(),
      repaired_in_B = logical(),
      keep_row = logical(),
      drop_row = logical(),
      collision_n_rows = integer(),
      keep_reason = character(),
      Progress = character(),
      Finished = character(),
      StartDate = character(),
      EndDate = character()
    )
    return(list(
      part2_clean = part2_df,
      collision_review = empty_review
    ))
  }

  part2_tagged <- part2_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
      repaired_in_B = row_id %in% repaired_row_ids
    )

  touched_ppns <- part2_tagged %>%
    dplyr::filter(repaired_in_B, !is_missing_ppn(ppn)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(ppn) %>%
    dplyr::pull(ppn)

  if (length(touched_ppns) == 0) {
    empty_review <- tibble::tibble(
      ppn = character(),
      row_id = integer(),
      repaired_in_B = logical(),
      keep_row = logical(),
      drop_row = logical(),
      collision_n_rows = integer(),
      keep_reason = character(),
      Progress = character(),
      Finished = character(),
      StartDate = character(),
      EndDate = character()
    )
    return(list(
      part2_clean = part2_df,
      collision_review = empty_review
    ))
  }

  collision_candidates <- part2_tagged %>%
    dplyr::filter(ppn %in% touched_ppns) %>%
    dplyr::add_count(ppn, name = "collision_n_rows") %>%
    dplyr::filter(collision_n_rows > 1)

  if (nrow(collision_candidates) == 0) {
    empty_review <- tibble::tibble(
      ppn = character(),
      row_id = integer(),
      repaired_in_B = logical(),
      keep_row = logical(),
      drop_row = logical(),
      collision_n_rows = integer(),
      keep_reason = character(),
      Progress = character(),
      Finished = character(),
      StartDate = character(),
      EndDate = character()
    )
    return(list(
      part2_clean = part2_df,
      collision_review = empty_review
    ))
  }

  collision_ranked <- collision_candidates %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Progress_rank = if ("Progress" %in% names(.)) normalize_progress(Progress) else -Inf,
      Finished_rank = if ("Finished" %in% names(.)) normalize_finished(Finished) else -Inf,
      EndDate_rank = if ("EndDate_posix" %in% names(.)) as.numeric(EndDate_posix) else -Inf,
      nonmissing_rank = safe_nonmissing_count(.)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(ppn) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(Progress_rank),
      dplyr::desc(Finished_rank),
      repaired_in_B,
      dplyr::desc(EndDate_rank),
      dplyr::desc(nonmissing_rank),
      row_id,
      .by_group = TRUE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      keep_row = dplyr::row_number() == 1,
      drop_row = !keep_row,
      keep_reason = dplyr::case_when(
        keep_row ~ "kept_highest_progress_then_finished_then_original_row_then_latest_enddate",
        TRUE ~ "dropped_postrepair_collision"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  rows_to_drop <- collision_ranked %>%
    dplyr::filter(drop_row) %>%
    dplyr::pull(row_id)

  part2_clean <- part2_tagged %>%
    dplyr::filter(!row_id %in% rows_to_drop) %>%
    dplyr::select(-row_id, -repaired_in_B)

  collision_review <- collision_ranked %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      ppn,
      row_id,
      repaired_in_B,
      keep_row,
      drop_row,
      collision_n_rows,
      keep_reason,
      Progress = if ("Progress" %in% names(collision_ranked)) as.character(Progress) else NA_character_,
      Finished = if ("Finished" %in% names(collision_ranked)) as.character(Finished) else NA_character_,
      StartDate = if ("StartDate" %in% names(collision_ranked)) as.character(StartDate) else NA_character_,
      EndDate = if ("EndDate" %in% names(collision_ranked)) as.character(EndDate) else NA_character_
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(ppn, dplyr::desc(keep_row), row_id)

  list(
    part2_clean = part2_clean,
    collision_review = collision_review
  )
}

# -------------------------
# 2) Standardize timestamps + key fields used for matching
#    (do not assume earlier sections have already created *_posix)
# -------------------------
part2_B <- part2 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

part1_B <- part1 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

sensitive_B <- sensitive %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate)
  )

financial_B <- financial_comp %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
    StartDate_posix = parse_dt_any(StartDate),
    EndDate_posix   = parse_dt_any(EndDate),
    fc_name = as.character(fc_name),
    fc_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(stringr::str_to_title(fc_name)),
    fc_name_clean = clean_name(fc_name_title),
    fin_row_id = dplyr::row_number()
  )

# Choose IC source post Step A test drops if present
ic_source <- if (exists("ic_combined_working")) ic_combined_working else ic_combined

ic_name_col <- dplyr::case_when(
  "Name" %in% names(ic_source) ~ "Name",
  "ic_name" %in% names(ic_source) ~ "ic_name",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)
stopifnot(!is.na(ic_name_col))

ic_lookup <- ic_source %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ResponseId = trimws(as.character(ResponseId)),
    ic_name_raw = as.character(.data[[ic_name_col]]),
    ic_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(stringr::str_to_title(ic_name_raw)),
    ic_name_clean = clean_name(ic_name_title)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ic_name_clean) & ic_name_clean != "" & !is.na(ResponseId) & ResponseId != "") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ic_name_clean) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    ic_name_title_values = paste(sort(unique(stats::na.omit(ic_name_title))), collapse = " | "),
    ic_responseids = paste(sort(unique(ResponseId)), collapse = " | "),
    n_ic_responseids = dplyr::n_distinct(ResponseId),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# For tie-breaking IC restarts, use existing Part 1 ppns (non-missing).
part1_ppn_pool <- unique(part1_B$ppn[!is_missing_ppn(part1_B$ppn)])

# -------------------------
# 3) Preflight: do we need any repairs?
# -------------------------
need_fix_part2 <- has_missing_ppn(part2_B, "ppn")
need_fix_part1 <- has_missing_ppn(part1_B, "ppn")
need_fix_sens  <- has_missing_ppn(sensitive_B, "ppn")

# Always create these objects so downstream code never fails after a clean run.
part2_review_tbl <- tibble::tibble()
part1_review_tbl <- tibble::tibble()
sens_review_tbl  <- tibble::tibble()

# -------------------------
# 4) Build Part 2 suggestions (closest to Financial anchor)
# -------------------------
if (need_fix_part2) {
  part2_missing <- part2_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_missing_ppn(ppn)) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      component = "part2",
      row_id,
      StartDate_posix,
      EndDate_posix,
      match_target_time = EndDate_posix
    )

  part2_review_tbl <- part2_missing %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      .m = list(time_match_one(match_target_time, financial_B$StartDate_posix, tolerance_secs)),
      fin_row_id = .m$best_index,
      fin_best_abs_diff = .m$best_abs_diff,
      fin_n_within_tol = .m$n_within_tol,
      fin_within_tol = !is.na(fin_row_id),

      fin_StartDate_posix = if (fin_within_tol) financial_B$StartDate_posix[fin_row_id] else as.POSIXct(NA),
      fin_EndDate_posix   = if (fin_within_tol) financial_B$EndDate_posix[fin_row_id] else as.POSIXct(NA),
      fin_name_title      = if (fin_within_tol) financial_B$fc_name_title[fin_row_id] else NA_character_,
      fin_name_clean      = if (fin_within_tol) financial_B$fc_name_clean[fin_row_id] else NA_character_,
      fin_ppn_raw         = if (fin_within_tol) financial_B$ppn[fin_row_id] else NA_character_,

      fin_time_diff_secs = if (fin_within_tol)
        as.numeric(difftime(fin_StartDate_posix, match_target_time, units = "secs"))
      else NA_real_
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::left_join(ic_lookup, by = c("fin_name_clean" = "ic_name_clean")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      suggestion_status = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(EndDate_posix) ~ "missing_part2_enddate",
        is.na(fin_row_id) ~ "no_financial_time_match",
        is.na(fin_name_clean) | fin_name_clean == "" ~ "financial_time_match_but_missing_name",
        is.na(ic_responseids) ~ "financial_name_not_found_in_ic",
        n_ic_responseids > 1 ~ "financial_name_maps_to_multiple_ic_ppns",
        n_ic_responseids == 1 ~ "unique_ic_ppn_recovered",
        TRUE ~ "unknown"
      ),

      ic_candidates_in_part1 = dplyr::case_when(
        suggestion_status == "financial_name_maps_to_multiple_ic_ppns" ~ purrr::map_chr(
          ic_responseids,
          ~{
            if (is.na(.x) || trimws(.x) == "") return("")
            cands <- stringr::str_split(.x, "\\s*\\|\\s*")[[1]]
            cands <- trimws(cands)
            hits <- cands[cands %in% part1_ppn_pool]
            if (length(hits) == 0) "" else paste(hits, collapse = " | ")
          }
        ),
        TRUE ~ ""
      ),

      n_candidates_in_part1 = dplyr::if_else(
        ic_candidates_in_part1 == "",
        0L,
        stringr::str_count(ic_candidates_in_part1, "\\|") + 1L
      ),

      suggested_ppn = dplyr::case_when(
        suggestion_status == "unique_ic_ppn_recovered" ~ ic_responseids,
        suggestion_status == "financial_name_maps_to_multiple_ic_ppns" & n_candidates_in_part1 == 1 ~ ic_candidates_in_part1,
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),

      suggestion_status = dplyr::case_when(
        suggestion_status == "financial_name_maps_to_multiple_ic_ppns" & n_candidates_in_part1 == 1 ~ "resolved_by_part1_presence",
        TRUE ~ suggestion_status
      ),

      recommend_apply = !is.na(suggested_ppn) & trimws(suggested_ppn) != ""
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      component, row_id,
      StartDate_posix, EndDate_posix,
      fin_row_id,
      fin_StartDate_posix, fin_EndDate_posix,
      fin_ppn_raw,
      fin_name_title, fin_name_clean,
      fin_time_diff_secs,
      fin_n_within_tol,
      ic_name_title_values, ic_responseids, n_ic_responseids,
      n_candidates_in_part1, ic_candidates_in_part1,
      suggested_ppn,
      suggestion_status,
      recommend_apply
    )
}

# -------------------------
# 5) Write ONE combined review file (even if empty)
# -------------------------
review_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  part2_review_tbl,
  part1_review_tbl,
  sens_review_tbl
)

review_out <- review_tbl %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    apply_fix = recommend_apply,
    ppn_new = "",
    notes = ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(component, dplyr::desc(recommend_apply))

if (nrow(review_out) == 0) {
  review_out <- tibble::tibble(
    component = character(),
    row_id = integer(),
    StartDate_posix = as.POSIXct(character()),
    EndDate_posix = as.POSIXct(character()),
    suggested_ppn = character(),
    suggestion_status = character(),
    recommend_apply = logical(),
    apply_fix = logical(),
    ppn_new = character(),
    notes = character()
  )
}

write_review_csv(review_out, "B_missing_ppn_review.csv")

# -------------------------
# 6) Re-import edited review + apply Part 2 fixes first
#    Then resolve post-repair Part 2 collisions before Part 1 proposals.
# -------------------------
review_edited <- read_audit_csv2("B_missing_ppn_review.csv") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    component = as.character(component),
    row_id = suppressWarnings(as.integer(row_id)),
    apply_fix = as.logical(apply_fix),
    ppn_new = as.character(ppn_new),
    suggested_ppn = as.character(suggested_ppn),
    ppn_to_apply = dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(ppn_new) & trimws(ppn_new) != "",
      trimws(ppn_new),
      trimws(suggested_ppn)
    )
  )

stopifnot(!any(is.na(review_edited$row_id)))

fixes_to_apply <- review_edited %>%
  dplyr::filter(apply_fix == TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "") %>%
  dplyr::select(component, row_id, ppn_to_apply, suggestion_status, recommend_apply, notes)

# Always define working outputs
part2_working <- part2_B
part1_working <- part1_B
sensitive_working <- sensitive_B

part2_collision_review <- tibble::tibble()

# ---- (1) apply Part 2 fixes ----
part2_fixes <- fixes_to_apply %>% dplyr::filter(component == "part2")

if (nrow(part2_fixes) > 0) {
  part2_working_pre_collision <- part2_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(part2_fixes %>% dplyr::select(row_id, ppn_to_apply), by = "row_id") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ppn_before = ppn,
      ppn = dplyr::if_else(
        is_missing_ppn(ppn) & !is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "",
        ppn_to_apply,
        ppn
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-ppn_to_apply)

  part2_receipt <- part2_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn_before = ppn) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(part2_fixes, by = "row_id") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      part2_working_pre_collision %>%
        dplyr::transmute(row_id, ppn_after = ppn),
      by = "row_id"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_missing_ppn(ppn_before) & !is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      component = "part2",
      row_id,
      ppn_before,
      ppn_after,
      ppn_to_apply,
      suggestion_status,
      recommend_apply,
      notes
    )

  write_receipt_csv(part2_receipt, "B_missing_ppn_receipt_part2.csv")

  part2_collision_res <- resolve_part2_postrepair_collisions(
    part2_df = part2_working_pre_collision %>% dplyr::select(-ppn_before),
    repaired_row_ids = part2_fixes$row_id
  )

  part2_working <- part2_collision_res$part2_clean
  part2_collision_review <- part2_collision_res$collision_review

  write_receipt_csv(part2_collision_review, "B_postrepair_collision_receipt_part2.csv")
} else {
  part2_working <- part2_B
  part2_collision_review <- tibble::tibble(
    ppn = character(),
    row_id = integer(),
    repaired_in_B = logical(),
    keep_row = logical(),
    drop_row = logical(),
    collision_n_rows = integer(),
    keep_reason = character(),
    Progress = character(),
    Finished = character(),
    StartDate = character(),
    EndDate = character()
  )
  write_receipt_csv(part2_collision_review, "B_postrepair_collision_receipt_part2.csv")
}

# -------------------------
# 7) Build Part 1 suggestions using repaired + collision-resolved Part 2
# -------------------------
part2_working_proposal <- part2_working %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
    ppn_proposed = ppn
  )

if (need_fix_part1) {
  part1_missing <- part1_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_missing_ppn(ppn)) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      component = "part1",
      row_id,
      StartDate_posix,
      EndDate_posix,
      match_target_time = EndDate_posix
    )

  part1_review_tbl <- part1_missing %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      .m = list(time_match_one(match_target_time, part2_working_proposal$StartDate_posix, tolerance_secs)),
      part2_row_id = .m$best_index,
      part2_best_abs_diff = .m$best_abs_diff,
      part2_n_within_tol = .m$n_within_tol,
      part2_within_tol = !is.na(part2_row_id),

      part2_StartDate_posix = if (part2_within_tol) part2_working_proposal$StartDate_posix[part2_row_id] else as.POSIXct(NA),
      part2_EndDate_posix   = if (part2_within_tol) part2_working_proposal$EndDate_posix[part2_row_id] else as.POSIXct(NA),
      part2_ppn_proposed    = if (part2_within_tol) part2_working_proposal$ppn_proposed[part2_row_id] else NA_character_,

      part2_time_diff_secs = if (part2_within_tol)
        as.numeric(difftime(part2_StartDate_posix, match_target_time, units = "secs"))
      else NA_real_
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      suggested_ppn = dplyr::case_when(
        part2_within_tol & !is.na(part2_ppn_proposed) & part2_ppn_proposed != "" ~ part2_ppn_proposed,
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      suggestion_status = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(EndDate_posix) ~ "missing_part1_enddate",
        is.na(part2_row_id) ~ "no_part2_time_match",
        is.na(part2_ppn_proposed) | part2_ppn_proposed == "" ~ "matched_part2_but_part2_ppn_unresolved",
        TRUE ~ "inherited_from_part2"
      ),
      recommend_apply = !is.na(suggested_ppn) & suggested_ppn != ""
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      component, row_id,
      StartDate_posix, EndDate_posix,
      part2_row_id,
      part2_StartDate_posix, part2_EndDate_posix,
      part2_ppn_proposed,
      part2_time_diff_secs,
      part2_n_within_tol,
      suggested_ppn,
      suggestion_status,
      recommend_apply
    )
}

# -------------------------
# 8) Build a Part 1 proposed map and apply Part 1 fixes
# -------------------------
if (nrow(part1_review_tbl) > 0 && "suggested_ppn" %in% names(part1_review_tbl)) {
  part1_suggested_map <- part1_review_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(suggested_ppn) & suggested_ppn != "") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      part1_row_id = row_id,
      part1_suggested_ppn = suggested_ppn,
      part1_suggestion_status = suggestion_status
    )
} else {
  part1_suggested_map <- tibble::tibble(
    part1_row_id = integer(),
    part1_suggested_ppn = character(),
    part1_suggestion_status = character()
  )
}

if (nrow(part1_suggested_map) > 0) {
  part1_working <- part1_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(part1_suggested_map, by = c("row_id" = "part1_row_id")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ppn_before = ppn,
      ppn = dplyr::if_else(
        is_missing_ppn(ppn) & !is.na(part1_suggested_ppn) & part1_suggested_ppn != "",
        part1_suggested_ppn,
        ppn
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-row_id, -part1_suggested_ppn, -part1_suggestion_status, -ppn_before)

  part1_receipt <- part1_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn_before = ppn) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(part1_suggested_map, by = c("row_id" = "part1_row_id")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      part1_working %>%
        dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn_after = ppn) %>%
        dplyr::select(row_id, ppn_after),
      by = "row_id"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_missing_ppn(ppn_before) & !is.na(part1_suggested_ppn) & part1_suggested_ppn != "") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      component = "part1",
      row_id,
      ppn_before,
      ppn_after,
      ppn_to_apply = part1_suggested_ppn,
      suggestion_status = part1_suggestion_status
    )

  write_receipt_csv(part1_receipt, "B_missing_ppn_receipt_part1.csv")
} else {
  part1_working <- part1_B
}

# -------------------------
# 9) Build Sensitive suggestions using repaired Part 1
# -------------------------
part1_working_proposal <- part1_working %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
    ppn_proposed = ppn
  )

if (need_fix_sens) {
  sens_missing <- sensitive_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_missing_ppn(ppn)) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      component = "sensitive",
      row_id,
      StartDate_posix,
      EndDate_posix,
      match_target_time = EndDate_posix
    )

  sens_review_tbl <- sens_missing %>%
    dplyr::rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      .m = list(time_match_one(match_target_time, part1_working_proposal$StartDate_posix, tolerance_secs)),
      part1_row_id = .m$best_index,
      part1_best_abs_diff = .m$best_abs_diff,
      part1_n_within_tol = .m$n_within_tol,
      part1_within_tol = !is.na(part1_row_id),

      part1_StartDate_posix = if (part1_within_tol) part1_working_proposal$StartDate_posix[part1_row_id] else as.POSIXct(NA),
      part1_EndDate_posix   = if (part1_within_tol) part1_working_proposal$EndDate_posix[part1_row_id] else as.POSIXct(NA),
      part1_ppn_proposed    = if (part1_within_tol) part1_working_proposal$ppn_proposed[part1_row_id] else NA_character_,

      part1_time_diff_secs = if (part1_within_tol)
        as.numeric(difftime(part1_StartDate_posix, match_target_time, units = "secs"))
      else NA_real_
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      suggested_ppn = dplyr::case_when(
        part1_within_tol & !is.na(part1_ppn_proposed) & part1_ppn_proposed != "" ~ part1_ppn_proposed,
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      suggestion_status = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(EndDate_posix) ~ "missing_sensitive_enddate",
        is.na(part1_row_id) ~ "no_part1_time_match",
        is.na(part1_ppn_proposed) | part1_ppn_proposed == "" ~ "matched_part1_but_part1_ppn_unresolved",
        TRUE ~ "inherited_from_part1"
      ),
      recommend_apply = !is.na(suggested_ppn) & suggested_ppn != ""
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      component, row_id,
      StartDate_posix, EndDate_posix,
      part1_row_id,
      part1_StartDate_posix, part1_EndDate_posix,
      part1_ppn_proposed,
      part1_time_diff_secs,
      part1_n_within_tol,
      suggested_ppn,
      suggestion_status,
      recommend_apply
    )
}

# -------------------------
# 10) Apply Sensitive fixes
# -------------------------
if (nrow(sens_review_tbl) > 0 && "suggested_ppn" %in% names(sens_review_tbl)) {
  sens_suggested_map <- sens_review_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(suggested_ppn) & suggested_ppn != "") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      sens_row_id = row_id,
      sens_suggested_ppn = suggested_ppn,
      sens_suggestion_status = suggestion_status
    )
} else {
  sens_suggested_map <- tibble::tibble(
    sens_row_id = integer(),
    sens_suggested_ppn = character(),
    sens_suggestion_status = character()
  )
}

if (nrow(sens_suggested_map) > 0) {
  sensitive_working <- sensitive_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sens_suggested_map, by = c("row_id" = "sens_row_id")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ppn_before = ppn,
      ppn = dplyr::if_else(
        is_missing_ppn(ppn) & !is.na(sens_suggested_ppn) & sens_suggested_ppn != "",
        sens_suggested_ppn,
        ppn
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-row_id, -sens_suggested_ppn, -sens_suggestion_status, -ppn_before)

  sens_receipt <- sensitive_B %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn_before = ppn) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(sens_suggested_map, by = c("row_id" = "sens_row_id")) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      sensitive_working %>%
        dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn_after = ppn) %>%
        dplyr::select(row_id, ppn_after),
      by = "row_id"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_missing_ppn(ppn_before) & !is.na(sens_suggested_ppn) & sens_suggested_ppn != "") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      component = "sensitive",
      row_id,
      ppn_before,
      ppn_after,
      ppn_to_apply = sens_suggested_ppn,
      suggestion_status = sens_suggestion_status
    )

  write_receipt_csv(sens_receipt, "B_missing_ppn_receipt_sensitive.csv")
} else {
  sensitive_working <- sensitive_B
}

# -------------------------
# 11) Final objects exported by this step (for downstream sections)
# -------------------------
# Use these moving forward:
#   - part2_working
#   - part1_working
#   - sensitive_working
#
# And keep these for audit traceability:
#   - part2_review_tbl
#   - part1_review_tbl
#   - sens_review_tbl
#   - part2_collision_review

```


Audit Step C: Resolve Shared PPN Collisions 

This audit step detects and repairs shared ppn collisions, where the same Qualtrics identifier (ppn) ends up being used by multiple different participants. These collisions typically occur when a survey link is shared, causing multiple individuals to submit responses under the same Qualtrics session identifier.

This is one of the most serious integrity problems in the pipeline, because it can silently collapse multiple distinct individuals into a single identity and contaminate downstream linkage, participation tracking, and any analyses that rely on person-level uniqueness.



Why Financial Is the Anchor for Collision Detection

The survey flow for each wave is:

IC → Sensitive → Part 1 → Part 2 → Financial

Financial is the best file for detecting shared ppn collisions because it is:

the final component in the survey chain

the only downstream file that reliably contains a participant name field

the most direct place to detect when one ppn is associated with multiple distinct names



A shared ppn collision is defined here as:

A single ppn in Financial that appears with more than one unique cleaned participant name (fc_name_clean).



Two Collision Scenarios We Handle

This step is written to detect and repair both collision patterns observed across waves.



Scenario 1: Collision participants exist in IC (standard case)

In this scenario, each participant completed Informed Consent, meaning their identity exists in IC.
If Financial shows that multiple names share the same ppn, we can map each Financial name back to IC and recover that participant’s correct canonical identifier (IC ResponseId).

This is the preferred resolution and preserves full linkage consistency.



Scenario 2: Collision participants do not exist in IC (shared link after IC)

In this scenario, the shared link occurs after IC, meaning one or more participants completed downstream components without ever generating an IC record. These participants still appear in Financial with a name, but there is no corresponding IC identity to map them to.

In this case, we generate a deterministic synthetic ppn so that the participant is still represented as a unique identity in downstream datasets.

This allows the pipeline to preserve uniqueness even when IC linkage is impossible.



High Level Strategy

Audit Step C follows a conservative and traceable process:

Detect shared ppns in Financial
We identify all ppn values in Financial that map to more than one unique participant name.

Use Financial to infer identity-specific ppn assignments
For each Financial row under a shared ppn, we determine whether that participant name can be linked back to IC.

Generate reassignment proposals for downstream survey rows
For each downstream row (Part 2, Part 1, Sensitive) that currently uses a shared ppn, we propose a corrected ppn by matching it to the nearest Financial row in time.

Resolve identity using IC when possible
If the matched Financial name maps back to IC, the proposed fix is reassignment to the participant’s IC canonical ppn.

Generate a synthetic ppn when IC linkage is impossible
If the Financial name does not exist in IC, a deterministic synthetic ppn is proposed instead.

Single review file, conservative application
All proposed reassignments are written to one editable review file. Fixes are applied only when explicitly approved.



Output of Step C

Audit Step C produces:

One review file (editable): C_shared_ppn_reassign_review.csv
This contains all proposed reassignment candidates across the relevant survey components.

Optional receipts (recommended for traceability): compact summaries of applied changes written separately from the review file.

By the end of Step C, shared ppn collisions are resolved in a way that preserves participant uniqueness and ensures downstream identity linkage remains valid.



```{r}
# -------------------------
###############################################################################
# AUDIT STEP C: shared ppn collisions (WRITE -> EDIT -> READ -> APPLY)
###############################################################################
# Goal:
#   Detect "shared ppn" collisions using Financial Compensation:
#     - if multiple different names appear under the same ppn in financial,
#       that ppn was likely a shared link / collision.
#
# IMPORTANT (wave generalization):
#   We handle TWO collision scenarios:
#
#   (1) "In IC" collision:
#       The financial name maps back to IC (via ic_ledger_working Name_clean),
#       so we can propose a reassignment to the IC ResponseId.
#
#   (2) "Post-IC shared link" collision:
#       The shared ppn was created AFTER IC (no IC name row exists),
#       so there is no IC ResponseId to recover.
#       In this case we propose a deterministic synthetic ppn based on the
#       shared ppn + the matched financial row id.
#
# Output strategy (minimal audit clutter):
#   - ONE editable review file:
#       C_shared_ppn_review.csv   (EDIT THIS: apply_fix / ppn_new / notes)
#   - Optional receipts written to a receipts subfolder:
#       audit_outputs/receipts/C_shared_ppn_applied.csv
#
# Working outputs (objects in R):
#   - part2_working2
#   - part1_working2
#   - sensitive_working2
#   - financial_working2
###############################################################################

# -------------------------
# Controls (edit as needed)
# -------------------------
include_part2     <- TRUE
include_part1     <- TRUE
include_sensitive <- TRUE

# Optional: also rewrite ppn inside financial for synthetic assignments
# (recommended only if you want financial rows to follow the synthetic identity)
include_financial <- TRUE

# If TRUE: block reads edited review file and applies changes
# If FALSE: block writes review file and stops
apply_shared_ppn_fixes <- TRUE

# Optional: flag "nearest match too far" (set Inf to disable)
shared_match_max_secs <- Inf

# Tolerance for matching within the same shared_ppn (in seconds)
# This is separate from Audit Step B tolerances and can be looser.
shared_match_tolerance_secs <- 60

# Deterministic prefix for synthetic ppns (edit if you want a different convention)
# Tip: include wave label if helpful (e.g., "SYN_T1_", "SYN_T2_")
synthetic_prefix <- "SYN_"

# -------------------------
# Preconditions + pick "working" inputs
# -------------------------
stopifnot(exists("audit_dir"))
stopifnot(exists("write_audit_csv"))
stopifnot(exists("read_audit_csv2"))
stopifnot(exists("clean_name"))
stopifnot(exists("fix_tussenvoegsels"))
stopifnot(exists("parse_dt_any"))

stopifnot(exists("ic_ledger_working"))

# Pick the best-available working datasets (robust to ordering changes)
part2_C <- if (exists("part2_working")) part2_working else if (exists("part2_B")) part2_B else part2
part1_C <- if (exists("part1_working")) part1_working else if (exists("part1_B")) part1_B else part1
sens_C  <- if (exists("sensitive_working")) sensitive_working else if (exists("sensitive_B")) sensitive_B else sensitive

# Financial after Step B can be named differently depending on your rewrite.
# Prefer financial_B if it exists (it should have parsed times already), else financial_comp.
financial_C <- if (exists("financial_B")) financial_B else financial_comp

# Ensure receipts folder exists
receipts_dir <- file.path(audit_dir, "receipts")
if (!dir.exists(receipts_dir)) dir.create(receipts_dir, recursive = TRUE)

write_receipt_csv <- function(df, filename) {
  out_path <- file.path(receipts_dir, filename)
  write.csv2(df, file = out_path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
  message("Wrote receipt: ", out_path)
  invisible(out_path)
}

# -------------------------
# Helper: pick a usable timestamp for a row
# -------------------------
get_row_time <- function(df, prefer = c("StartDate_posix", "EndDate_posix", "RecordedDate")) {
  for (nm in prefer) {
    if (nm %in% names(df)) {
      x <- df[[nm]]
      if (nm == "RecordedDate" && !inherits(x, "POSIXct")) x <- parse_dt_any(x)
      if (inherits(x, "POSIXct")) return(x)
    }
  }
  as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC")
}

# -------------------------
# Helper: deterministic synthetic ppn
# -------------------------
make_synth_ppn <- function(shared_ppn, fin_row_id) {
  paste0(
    synthetic_prefix,
    trimws(as.character(shared_ppn)),
    "_",
    sprintf("%05d", as.integer(fin_row_id))
  )
}

# -------------------------
# 1) Standardize financial & detect shared ppns
# -------------------------
stopifnot("ppn" %in% names(financial_C))

financial_C_std <- financial_C %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
    fc_name = if ("fc_name" %in% names(.)) as.character(fc_name) else if ("Name" %in% names(.)) as.character(Name) else NA_character_,
    fc_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(stringr::str_to_title(fc_name)),
    fc_name_clean = clean_name(fc_name_title),
    fin_time = get_row_time(., prefer = c("StartDate_posix", "EndDate_posix", "RecordedDate")),
    fin_row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
    fin_ip = if ("IPAddress" %in% names(.)) as.character(IPAddress) else NA_character_
  )

shared_ppn_summary <- financial_C_std %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn) & ppn != "") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ppn) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_names = dplyr::n_distinct(fc_name_clean),
    fc_names = paste(sort(unique(stats::na.omit(fc_name_title))), collapse = " | "),
    n_rows = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_names > 1) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_names), dplyr::desc(n_rows))

shared_ppns <- shared_ppn_summary$ppn

# If none, write an empty review file and pass-through working objects
if (length(shared_ppns) == 0) {

  message("No shared ppns detected in financial. Skipping Audit Step C.")

  empty_review <- tibble::tibble(
    dataset = character(),
    row_id = integer(),
    shared_ppn = character(),
    row_time = as.POSIXct(character(), tz = "UTC"),
    row_ip = character(),

    fin_row_id = integer(),
    fin_time = as.POSIXct(character(), tz = "UTC"),
    fin_ip = character(),
    fin_name_title = character(),
    fin_name_clean = character(),
    fin_time_diff_secs = numeric(),

    ic_responseids = character(),
    n_ic_responseids = integer(),
    ic_name_title_values = character(),

    suggested_ppn = character(),
    suggested_type = character(),
    suggestion_status = character(),
    recommend_apply = logical(),

    apply_fix = logical(),
    ppn_new = character(),
    notes = character()
  )

  write_audit_csv(empty_review, "C_shared_ppn_review.csv")

  part2_working2 <- part2_C
  part1_working2 <- part1_C
  sensitive_working2 <- sens_C
  financial_working2 <- financial_C_std

} else {

  # -------------------------
  # 2) Build IC name -> ResponseId lookup (NO identity_roster needed)
  # -------------------------
  ic_lookup_C <- ic_ledger_working %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ResponseId = trimws(as.character(ResponseId)),
      Name_clean = as.character(Name_clean),
      Name_title = as.character(Name_title)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Name_clean) & Name_clean != "" & !is.na(ResponseId) & ResponseId != "") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Name_clean) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      ic_name_title_values = paste(sort(unique(stats::na.omit(Name_title))), collapse = " | "),
      ic_responseids = paste(sort(unique(ResponseId)), collapse = " | "),
      n_ic_responseids = dplyr::n_distinct(ResponseId),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # -------------------------
  # 3) Candidate downstream rows that currently use a shared ppn
  # -------------------------
  candidates <- tibble::tibble()

  if (include_part2) {
    c2 <- part2_C %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        dataset = "part2",
        row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
        ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
        row_time = get_row_time(., prefer = c("EndDate_posix", "StartDate_posix", "RecordedDate")),
        row_ip = if ("IPAddress" %in% names(.)) as.character(IPAddress) else NA_character_
      ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn) & ppn != "" & ppn %in% shared_ppns) %>%
      dplyr::select(dataset, row_id, shared_ppn = ppn, row_time, row_ip)

    candidates <- dplyr::bind_rows(candidates, c2)
  }

  if (include_part1) {
    c1 <- part1_C %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        dataset = "part1",
        row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
        ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
        row_time = get_row_time(., prefer = c("EndDate_posix", "StartDate_posix", "RecordedDate")),
        row_ip = if ("IPAddress" %in% names(.)) as.character(IPAddress) else NA_character_
      ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn) & ppn != "" & ppn %in% shared_ppns) %>%
      dplyr::select(dataset, row_id, shared_ppn = ppn, row_time, row_ip)

    candidates <- dplyr::bind_rows(candidates, c1)
  }

  if (include_sensitive) {
    cs <- sens_C %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        dataset = "sensitive",
        row_id = dplyr::row_number(),
        ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
        row_time = get_row_time(., prefer = c("EndDate_posix", "StartDate_posix", "RecordedDate")),
        row_ip = if ("IPAddress" %in% names(.)) as.character(IPAddress) else NA_character_
      ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn) & ppn != "" & ppn %in% shared_ppns) %>%
      dplyr::select(dataset, row_id, shared_ppn = ppn, row_time, row_ip)

    candidates <- dplyr::bind_rows(candidates, cs)
  }

  # If shared ppns exist but no downstream rows use them, write empty review + pass-through
  if (nrow(candidates) == 0) {

    message("Shared ppns found in financial, but no downstream rows use them in the selected datasets.")

    empty_review <- tibble::tibble(
      dataset = character(),
      row_id = integer(),
      shared_ppn = character(),
      row_time = as.POSIXct(character(), tz = "UTC"),
      row_ip = character(),

      fin_row_id = integer(),
      fin_time = as.POSIXct(character(), tz = "UTC"),
      fin_ip = character(),
      fin_name_title = character(),
      fin_name_clean = character(),
      fin_time_diff_secs = numeric(),

      ic_responseids = character(),
      n_ic_responseids = integer(),
      ic_name_title_values = character(),

      suggested_ppn = character(),
      suggested_type = character(),
      suggestion_status = character(),
      recommend_apply = logical(),

      apply_fix = logical(),
      ppn_new = character(),
      notes = character()
    )

    write_audit_csv(empty_review, "C_shared_ppn_review.csv")

    part2_working2 <- part2_C
    part1_working2 <- part1_C
    sensitive_working2 <- sens_C
    financial_working2 <- financial_C_std

  } else {

    # -------------------------
    # 4) Build ONE review table:
    #    For each candidate row, time-match to a financial row within the SAME shared_ppn,
    #    then:
    #      - if financial name maps to exactly one IC ResponseId -> propose that IC ppn
    #      - else if financial name not in IC (but exists) -> propose synthetic ppn
    #      - else -> leave unresolved for manual review
    # -------------------------
    fin_sub <- financial_C_std %>%
      dplyr::filter(ppn %in% shared_ppns) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(fin_time_num = as.numeric(fin_time))

    review_tbl <- candidates %>%
      dplyr::mutate(row_time_num = as.numeric(row_time)) %>%
      dplyr::rowwise() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        # subset indices for this shared ppn
        .idx = list(which(fin_sub$ppn == shared_ppn)),

        n_fin_rows_for_shared = length(.idx),

        best_fin_idx = {
          idx <- .idx[[1]]
          if (length(idx) == 0 || is.na(row_time_num)) NA_integer_ else {
            d <- abs(fin_sub$fin_time_num[idx] - row_time_num)
            idx[which.min(d)]
          }
        },

        best_dt_secs = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx) && !is.na(row_time_num))
          abs(fin_sub$fin_time_num[best_fin_idx] - row_time_num)
        else
          NA_real_,

        fin_row_id = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx)) fin_sub$fin_row_id[best_fin_idx] else NA_integer_,
        fin_time   = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx)) fin_sub$fin_time[best_fin_idx] else as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"),
        fin_ip     = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx)) fin_sub$fin_ip[best_fin_idx] else NA_character_,
        fin_name_title = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx)) fin_sub$fc_name_title[best_fin_idx] else NA_character_,
        fin_name_clean = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx)) fin_sub$fc_name_clean[best_fin_idx] else NA_character_,

        fin_time_diff_secs = if (!is.na(best_fin_idx) && !is.na(row_time))
          as.numeric(difftime(fin_time, row_time, units = "secs"))
        else
          NA_real_
      ) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::left_join(ic_lookup_C, by = c("fin_name_clean" = "Name_clean")) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        suggestion_status = dplyr::case_when(
          is.na(row_time) ~ "missing_row_time",
          n_fin_rows_for_shared == 0 ~ "no_financial_rows_for_shared_ppn",
          is.na(fin_row_id) ~ "no_financial_match_found",
          is.finite(shared_match_max_secs) & !is.na(best_dt_secs) & best_dt_secs > shared_match_max_secs ~ "nearest_match_too_far_flag",
          is.na(fin_name_clean) | fin_name_clean == "" ~ "financial_match_missing_name",
          is.na(n_ic_responseids) ~ "financial_name_not_found_in_ic",
          n_ic_responseids > 1 ~ "financial_name_maps_to_multiple_ic_ppns",
          n_ic_responseids == 1 ~ "unique_match_reassign_to_ic_ppn",
          TRUE ~ "unknown"
        ),

        suggested_ppn = dplyr::case_when(
          suggestion_status == "unique_match_reassign_to_ic_ppn" ~ ic_responseids,
          suggestion_status == "financial_name_not_found_in_ic" & !is.na(fin_name_clean) & fin_name_clean != "" & !is.na(fin_row_id) ~
            make_synth_ppn(shared_ppn, fin_row_id),
          TRUE ~ ""
        ),

        suggested_type = dplyr::case_when(
          suggestion_status == "unique_match_reassign_to_ic_ppn" ~ "ic",
          suggestion_status == "financial_name_not_found_in_ic" & suggested_ppn != "" ~ "synthetic",
          TRUE ~ "none"
        ),

        recommend_apply = suggested_ppn != "",

        # Editable decision fields
        apply_fix = recommend_apply,
        ppn_new = "",
        notes = ""
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(
        dataset, row_id, shared_ppn,
        row_time, row_ip,

        fin_row_id, fin_time, fin_ip,
        fin_name_title, fin_name_clean,
        fin_time_diff_secs,

        ic_responseids, n_ic_responseids, ic_name_title_values,

        suggested_ppn, suggested_type,
        suggestion_status, recommend_apply,

        apply_fix, ppn_new, notes
      ) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(shared_ppn, suggestion_status, dplyr::desc(recommend_apply), abs(fin_time_diff_secs))

    # Optional: flag ambiguous cases within a practical tolerance window
    # (This is just extra evidence, does not change suggested_ppn)
    review_tbl <- review_tbl %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    within_match_tolerance = !is.na(fin_time_diff_secs) &
      abs(fin_time_diff_secs) <= shared_match_tolerance_secs
  )


    write_review_csv(review_tbl, "C_shared_ppn_review.csv")

    if (!apply_shared_ppn_fixes) {
      stop(
        "Audit Step C review file written: C_shared_ppn_review.csv\n",
        "Edit apply_fix / ppn_new / notes as needed.\n",
        "Then set apply_shared_ppn_fixes <- TRUE and re-run Audit Step C."
      )
    }

    # -------------------------
    # 5) APPLY: read edited review file and apply approved changes
    # -------------------------
    review_edited <- read_audit_csv2("C_shared_ppn_review.csv") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        dataset = as.character(dataset),
        row_id = as.integer(row_id),
        shared_ppn = as.character(shared_ppn),
        apply_fix = as.logical(apply_fix),
        ppn_new = as.character(ppn_new),
        suggested_ppn = as.character(suggested_ppn),
        suggested_type = as.character(suggested_type),
        fin_row_id = suppressWarnings(as.integer(fin_row_id))
      )

    # Guardrails: reviewer should not reorder or delete rows
    stopifnot(nrow(review_edited) == nrow(review_tbl))
    stopifnot(all(review_edited$dataset == review_tbl$dataset))
    stopifnot(all(review_edited$row_id == review_tbl$row_id))
    stopifnot(all(review_edited$shared_ppn == review_tbl$shared_ppn))

    applied <- review_edited %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        ppn_to_apply = dplyr::case_when(
          !is.na(ppn_new) & ppn_new != "" ~ ppn_new,
          !is.na(suggested_ppn) & suggested_ppn != "" ~ suggested_ppn,
          TRUE ~ ""
        )
      ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(apply_fix == TRUE) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "") %>%
      dplyr::select(dataset, row_id, shared_ppn, ppn_to_apply, suggested_type, fin_row_id, suggestion_status, notes)

    # Receipt (kept out of audit root to reduce clutter)
    write_receipt_csv(applied, "C_shared_ppn_applied.csv")

    # Apply to datasets
    part2_working2 <- part2_C
    part1_working2 <- part1_C
    sensitive_working2 <- sens_C
    financial_working2 <- financial_C_std

    if (include_part2) {
      part2_working2 <- part2_C %>%
        dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn))) %>%
        dplyr::left_join(applied %>% dplyr::filter(dataset == "part2") %>% dplyr::select(row_id, ppn_to_apply), by = "row_id") %>%
        dplyr::mutate(ppn = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "", ppn_to_apply, ppn)) %>%
        dplyr::select(-row_id, -ppn_to_apply)
    }

    if (include_part1) {
      part1_working2 <- part1_C %>%
        dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn))) %>%
        dplyr::left_join(applied %>% dplyr::filter(dataset == "part1") %>% dplyr::select(row_id, ppn_to_apply), by = "row_id") %>%
        dplyr::mutate(ppn = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "", ppn_to_apply, ppn)) %>%
        dplyr::select(-row_id, -ppn_to_apply)
    }

    if (include_sensitive) {
      sensitive_working2 <- sens_C %>%
        dplyr::mutate(row_id = dplyr::row_number(), ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn))) %>%
        dplyr::left_join(applied %>% dplyr::filter(dataset == "sensitive") %>% dplyr::select(row_id, ppn_to_apply), by = "row_id") %>%
        dplyr::mutate(ppn = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "", ppn_to_apply, ppn)) %>%
        dplyr::select(-row_id, -ppn_to_apply)
    }

    # Optional: also apply synthetic ppns to financial by fin_row_id
    if (include_financial) {
      fin_apply <- applied %>%
        dplyr::filter(suggested_type == "synthetic") %>%
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(fin_row_id)) %>%
        dplyr::distinct(fin_row_id, ppn_to_apply)

      if (nrow(fin_apply) > 0) {
        financial_working2 <- financial_working2 %>%
          dplyr::left_join(fin_apply, by = "fin_row_id") %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ppn = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(ppn_to_apply) & ppn_to_apply != "", ppn_to_apply, ppn)) %>%
          dplyr::select(-ppn_to_apply)
      }
    }
  }
}

###############################################################################
# End result:
#   - part2_working2 / part1_working2 / sensitive_working2 have corrected ppns
#   - financial_working2 is standardized and optionally updated (if enabled)
#   - No dependency on identity_roster (since restarter resolution happens later)
###############################################################################


```


Audit Step D: Resolve IC Restarters Using Downstream Evidence

This step handles a common Qualtrics pattern where a participant submits Informed Consent more than once, creating multiple IC ResponseIds under the same cleaned name. We refer to these cases as IC restarters.

In this project, the IC ResponseId functions as the wave’s canonical participant identifier (ppn) that is intended to propagate across all downstream survey components. When restarts occur, we must choose one canonical IC ResponseId per identity so that linkage is stable and each person has a single ppn in the cleaned outputs.



What is already “clean” before Step D

Step D assumes the pipeline has already applied the earlier audit work:

Audit Step A (tests): test and researcher entries have been flagged and removed from the working IC universe and from downstream datasets where ppn propagates.

Audit Step B (missing ppns): missing ppn values in Sensitive, Part 1, and Part 2 have been repaired as much as possible using the backward, Financial anchored strategy. This matters because restarter resolution relies on downstream presence.

Audit Step C (shared ppn collisions): shared link collisions have been detected and repaired.
