Where collisions produced identities that never existed in IC, synthetic ppns may have been created and the downstream data updated accordingly. Step D does not create synthetic identities; it focuses only on resolving multiple IC ResponseIds that share the same name.

Because these earlier steps improve ppn completeness and remove known contamination, the downstream evidence used here is maximally informative and the resulting identity ledger is more reliable.



How Step D works

Detect restarters: identify name clusters in IC where the same cleaned name appears with more than one IC ResponseId.

Compute downstream evidence per candidate ResponseId: for each ResponseId in a restarter cluster, check whether it appears in the cleaned downstream components (Sensitive, Part 1, Part 2, Financial). We also check whether the person appears in Financial by name as a best effort signal.

Select an automatic canonical ppn: choose the ResponseId with the strongest downstream evidence (a weighted score) as the default canonical ppn.



Create two outputs:

a full identity ledger (read only, one row per person) for tracking participation and auditing decisions.

a small review queue (editable) containing only restart cases that are ambiguous or low signal (ties, very low evidence, or test flagged edge cases).

Apply reviewer decisions to produce identity_roster: the final roster contains exactly one canonical ppn per identity (canonical_responseid_final) and is the key object used for all downstream merging and export.



Outputs produced by Step D

D_identity_ledger.csv (read only): complete identity ledger for the wave (one row per name).

D_identity_review_queue.csv (editable): only restart cases that require manual review.

D_identity_review_applied.csv (receipt): only identities where a reviewer overrode or dropped the auto decision.



By the end of Step D, the pipeline has a clean, wave specific identity_roster that can be used to propagate canonical ppns across survey components and to support later completeness and export steps.


```{r}
# AUDIT STEP D: IC restarters (same name, multiple IC ResponseIds)
###############################################################################
# Purpose:
#   Detect IC "restarts" (same cleaned name submitted IC more than once) and use
#   downstream evidence to select ONE canonical IC ResponseId per identity.
#
# Key idea:
#   IC ResponseId is treated as the wave canonical participant identifier (ppn).
#   When a person restarts IC, we must choose a single canonical ResponseId so
#   that all downstream linkage is stable.
#
#   In addition, some participants may not have a usable IC identity row but do
#   have a synthetic ppn assigned in Step C plus a valid financial-comp name.
#   These synthetic-only participants should also be included in the full
#   identity ledger so that later linkage (Step F) can use:
#     - Name_title                  -> to connect to gutsID
#     - canonical_responseid_final  -> to propagate downstream
#
# Inputs expected to exist by this stage:
#   - ic_ledger_working  (IC after Audit Step A test removals)
#   - part1_working2     (after missing ppn repairs and shared ppn repairs)
#   - part2_working2
#   - sensitive_working2
#   - financial_working2
#
# Output strategy (audit_dir):
#   - D_identity_ledger.csv        (read only, one row per identity)
#   - D_identity_review_queue.csv  (editable, only restart cases needing review)
#
# Receipt output (receipts_dir if available, otherwise audit_dir):
#   - D_identity_review_applied.csv  (only override and drop decisions)
#
# Review decisions (editable in D_identity_review_queue.csv):
#   - decision: accept / override / drop
#   - canonical_responseid_final: fill only if decision == override
#   - drop_reason, notes
###############################################################################

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0) Pick working datasets with safe fallbacks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(exists("ic_ledger_working"))

part1_D <- if (exists("part1_working2")) part1_working2 else if (exists("part1_working")) part1_working else part1
part2_D <- if (exists("part2_working2")) part2_working2 else if (exists("part2_working")) part2_working else part2
sens_D  <- if (exists("sensitive_working2")) sensitive_working2 else if (exists("sensitive_working")) sensitive_working else sensitive
fin_D   <- if (exists("financial_working2")) financial_working2 else if (exists("financial_working_B")) financial_working_B else financial_comp

# Normalize ppn vectors for presence checks
part1_ppn_vec <- unique(trimws(as.character(part1_D$ppn)))
part2_ppn_vec <- unique(trimws(as.character(part2_D$ppn)))
sens_ppn_vec  <- unique(trimws(as.character(sens_D$ppn)))
fin_ppn_vec   <- unique(trimws(as.character(fin_D$ppn)))

# Normalize financial names if not already present
if (!("fc_name_clean" %in% names(fin_D))) {
  fin_D <- fin_D %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
      fc_name = if ("fc_name" %in% names(.)) as.character(fc_name) else if ("Name" %in% names(.)) as.character(Name) else NA_character_,
      fc_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(stringr::str_to_title(fc_name)),
      fc_name_clean = clean_name(fc_name_title)
    )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Build ic_presence table: one row per IC ResponseId candidate
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ic_presence <- ic_ledger_working %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Name_clean, Name_title, ResponseId, flag_test_by_date, flag_test_by_name, StartDate_posix) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ResponseId = trimws(as.character(ResponseId)),
    in_part1   = ResponseId %in% part1_ppn_vec,
    in_part2   = ResponseId %in% part2_ppn_vec,
    in_sens    = ResponseId %in% sens_ppn_vec,
    in_fc_ppn  = ResponseId %in% fin_ppn_vec,
    in_fc_name = !is.na(Name_clean) & Name_clean != "" & (Name_clean %in% unique(fin_D$fc_name_clean))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    downstream_score =
      (in_part1 * 2L) +
      (in_part2 * 2L) +
      (in_sens  * 1L) +
      (in_fc_ppn * 1L) +
      (in_fc_name * 1L)
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Rank candidate ResponseIds within each Name_clean cluster
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ic_ranked <- ic_presence %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Name_clean) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(downstream_score), StartDate_posix, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_ic_rows_for_name = dplyr::n(),
    canonical_responseid_auto = dplyr::first(ResponseId),
    canonical_score_auto      = downstream_score[match(canonical_responseid_auto, ResponseId)],
    is_canonical_auto = ResponseId == canonical_responseid_auto
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3a) IC-based identity ledger: one row per IC identity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
identity_ledger_ic <- ic_ranked %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Name_clean) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Name_title = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(Name_title)),
    n_ic_rows  = dplyr::first(n_ic_rows_for_name),

    canonical_responseid_auto = dplyr::first(canonical_responseid_auto),
    canonical_score_auto      = dplyr::first(canonical_score_auto),

    max_score = suppressWarnings(max(downstream_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_at_max  = suppressWarnings(sum(downstream_score == max_score, na.rm = TRUE)),

    ic_start_min = suppressWarnings(min(StartDate_posix, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ic_start_max = suppressWarnings(max(StartDate_posix, na.rm = TRUE)),

    any_test_flags = any(flag_test_by_date | flag_test_by_name, na.rm = TRUE),

    n_candidates_in_part1  = sum(in_part1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_candidates_in_part2  = sum(in_part2, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_candidates_in_sens   = sum(in_sens,  na.rm = TRUE),
    n_candidates_in_fc_ppn = sum(in_fc_ppn, na.rm = TRUE),
    in_fc_by_name          = any(in_fc_name, na.rm = TRUE),

    all_responseids = paste(ResponseId, collapse = " | "),
    scores_by_responseid = paste0(ResponseId, ":", downstream_score) %>% paste(collapse = " | "),
    part1_by_responseid  = paste0(ResponseId, ":", as.integer(in_part1)) %>% paste(collapse = " | "),
    part2_by_responseid  = paste0(ResponseId, ":", as.integer(in_part2)) %>% paste(collapse = " | "),
    sens_by_responseid   = paste0(ResponseId, ":", as.integer(in_sens))  %>% paste(collapse = " | "),

    reason_summary = dplyr::case_when(
      n_ic_rows == 1 ~ "single_ic_row",
      n_ic_rows > 1 & any(downstream_score > 0, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "multiple_ic_rows_pick_best_downstream",
      n_ic_rows > 1 ~ "multiple_ic_rows_no_downstream_signal",
      TRUE ~ "unknown"
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ic_start_min = dplyr::if_else(is.infinite(ic_start_min), as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"), ic_start_min),
    ic_start_max = dplyr::if_else(is.infinite(ic_start_max), as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"), ic_start_max),

    flag_restart    = n_ic_rows > 1,
    flag_tie_at_max = flag_restart & n_at_max > 1,
    flag_low_signal = canonical_score_auto == 0,

    auto_ok = canonical_score_auto >= 7 & !flag_tie_at_max & !any_test_flags,

    review_priority = dplyr::case_when(
      any_test_flags ~ "review_high_test",
      flag_tie_at_max ~ "review_high_tie",
      canonical_score_auto == 0 ~ "review_high_no_signal",
      canonical_score_auto < 7 ~ "review_medium_low_score",
      TRUE ~ "auto_ok"
    )
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3b) Synthetic-only identities from post-Step-C downstream data
#     These participants have a synthetic ppn and a usable financial-comp name,
#     but no usable IC identity row.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
synthetic_identity_ledger <- fin_D %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
    fc_name_title = as.character(fc_name_title),
    fc_name_clean = as.character(fc_name_clean)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(ppn),
    ppn != "",
    stringr::str_starts(ppn, synthetic_prefix),
    !is.na(fc_name_clean),
    fc_name_clean != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(ppn, fc_name_clean, fc_name_title) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    in_part1   = ppn %in% part1_ppn_vec,
    in_part2   = ppn %in% part2_ppn_vec,
    in_sens    = ppn %in% sens_ppn_vec,
    in_fc_ppn  = ppn %in% fin_ppn_vec,
    in_fc_name = TRUE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    downstream_score =
      (in_part1 * 2L) +
      (in_part2 * 2L) +
      (in_sens  * 1L) +
      (in_fc_ppn * 1L) +
      (in_fc_name * 1L)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Name_clean = fc_name_clean,
    Name_title = fc_name_title,
    n_ic_rows  = 0L,

    canonical_responseid_auto = ppn,
    canonical_score_auto      = downstream_score,

    max_score = downstream_score,
    n_at_max  = 1L,

    ic_start_min = as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"),
    ic_start_max = as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"),

    any_test_flags = FALSE,

    n_candidates_in_part1  = as.integer(in_part1),
    n_candidates_in_part2  = as.integer(in_part2),
    n_candidates_in_sens   = as.integer(in_sens),
    n_candidates_in_fc_ppn = as.integer(in_fc_ppn),
    in_fc_by_name          = TRUE,

    all_responseids = ppn,
    scores_by_responseid = paste0(ppn, ":", downstream_score),
    part1_by_responseid  = paste0(ppn, ":", as.integer(in_part1)),
    part2_by_responseid  = paste0(ppn, ":", as.integer(in_part2)),
    sens_by_responseid   = paste0(ppn, ":", as.integer(in_sens)),

    reason_summary = "synthetic_financial_only",

    flag_restart    = FALSE,
    flag_tie_at_max = FALSE,
    flag_low_signal = canonical_score_auto == 0,

    auto_ok = canonical_score_auto >= 7,

    review_priority = dplyr::case_when(
      canonical_score_auto == 0 ~ "review_high_no_signal",
      canonical_score_auto < 7 ~ "review_medium_low_score",
      TRUE ~ "auto_ok"
    )
  )

# If an IC identity already exists for the same Name_clean, keep the IC identity
synthetic_identity_ledger <- synthetic_identity_ledger %>%
  dplyr::filter(!(Name_clean %in% identity_ledger_ic$Name_clean))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3c) Final identity ledger: IC identities + synthetic-only identities
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
identity_ledger <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  identity_ledger_ic,
  synthetic_identity_ledger
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(review_priority, Name_title)

write_audit_csv(identity_ledger, "D_identity_ledger.csv")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Restart only review queue: editable, only the cases needing review
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
identity_review_queue_template <- identity_ledger %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    flag_restart == TRUE,
    review_priority != "auto_ok"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Name_title,
    Name_clean,

    n_ic_rows,
    canonical_responseid_auto,
    canonical_score_auto,
    max_score,
    n_at_max,

    ic_start_min,
    ic_start_max,

    n_candidates_in_part1,
    n_candidates_in_part2,
    n_candidates_in_sens,
    n_candidates_in_fc_ppn,
    in_fc_by_name,

    all_responseids,
    scores_by_responseid,
    part1_by_responseid,
    part2_by_responseid,
    sens_by_responseid,

    any_test_flags,
    reason_summary,
    flag_tie_at_max,
    flag_low_signal,
    review_priority,

    decision = "accept",
    canonical_responseid_final = "",
    drop_reason = "",
    notes = ""
  )

write_review_csv(identity_review_queue_template, "D_identity_review_queue.csv")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Re import decisions and apply to produce identity_roster
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
identity_review_queue <- read_audit_csv2("D_identity_review_queue.csv")

# Safety checks: reviewer should not reorder or delete rows
stopifnot(nrow(identity_review_queue) == nrow(identity_review_queue_template))
stopifnot(all(identity_review_queue$Name_clean == identity_review_queue_template$Name_clean))
stopifnot(all(identity_review_queue$canonical_responseid_auto == identity_review_queue_template$canonical_responseid_auto))

identity_roster <- identity_ledger %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    identity_review_queue %>%
      dplyr::select(Name_clean, decision, canonical_responseid_final, drop_reason, notes),
    by = "Name_clean"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    decision = dplyr::if_else(is.na(decision) | decision == "", "accept", as.character(decision)),

    canonical_responseid_final = dplyr::case_when(
      decision == "override" &
        !is.na(canonical_responseid_final) &
        canonical_responseid_final != "" ~ as.character(canonical_responseid_final),

      decision == "accept" ~ as.character(canonical_responseid_auto),

      decision == "drop" ~ NA_character_,

      TRUE ~ as.character(canonical_responseid_auto)
    ),

    override_is_valid = dplyr::if_else(
      decision == "override" &
        !is.na(canonical_responseid_final) &
        canonical_responseid_final != "",
      stringr::str_detect(all_responseids, stringr::fixed(canonical_responseid_final)),
      TRUE
    )
  )

stopifnot(all(identity_roster$override_is_valid))

# Receipt: only rows where reviewer changed something
identity_review_applied <- identity_roster %>%
  dplyr::filter(decision %in% c("override", "drop")) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Name_title, Name_clean,
    decision,
    canonical_responseid_auto, canonical_score_auto,
    canonical_responseid_final,
    drop_reason, notes,
    n_ic_rows, all_responseids, scores_by_responseid,
    review_priority, flag_tie_at_max, flag_low_signal, any_test_flags
  )

if (exists("write_receipt_csv")) {
  write_receipt_csv(identity_review_applied, "D_identity_review_applied.csv")
} else {
  write_audit_csv(identity_review_applied, "D_identity_review_applied.csv")
}

###############################################################################
# End result:
#   identity_roster contains canonical_responseid_final (ppn) for all retained
#   identities, including synthetic-only financial participants.
#   This will be used in later steps to propagate canonical ppns and to build
#   completeness and shareable exports.
###############################################################################


```


Audit Step E: Incompletes Ledger and Optional Exclusion

This audit step produces a single review file containing only incomplete / low signal identities, defined as anyone with canonical_score_auto < 7 (regardless of reason_summary). The goal is to create a formal record of incomplete participation with stage level evidence, while also providing a controlled way to remove identities that have no usable survey data.



Key behaviors

Who appears in the audit file
Only identities with canonical_score_auto < 7.



Auto decisions in the review file
If an identity has IC only (no rows in Sensitive, Part 1, Part 2, or Financial), it is auto marked keep = FALSE.
If an identity has any usable downstream data, it is auto marked keep = TRUE but still included with detailed completion evidence.



Applying removals
If any identities are removed, the script filters them out of the working datasets and then rebuilds identity_ledger and identity_roster so the objects used for linkage do not include removed subjects.


```{r}
# AUDIT STEP E: incompletes (canonical_score_auto < 7) + optional exclusion
###############################################################################
# Output strategy:
#   - One audit file (editable, in audit_dir):
#       E_incompletes_review.csv
#   - One receipt file (read-only, in receipts_dir):
#       E_incompletes_receipt.csv
#
# Rules:
#   - The audit file contains ONLY incompletes (canonical_score_auto < 7)
#   - IC-only identities are default keep = FALSE
#   - Any identity with any downstream rows defaults keep = TRUE
#   - If any are dropped, rebuild identity_ledger and identity_roster in place
#   - Critically, if any are dropped, also propagate the filtered datasets back
#     into the downstream working objects used by later steps
###############################################################################

stopifnot(exists("identity_ledger"))
stopifnot(exists("identity_roster"))
stopifnot(exists("ic_ledger_working"))
stopifnot(exists("write_audit_csv"))
stopifnot(exists("write_receipt_csv"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0) Choose most current working datasets
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
p1_E   <- if (exists("part1_working2")) part1_working2 else if (exists("part1_working")) part1_working else part1
p2_E   <- if (exists("part2_working2")) part2_working2 else if (exists("part2_working")) part2_working else part2
sens_E <- if (exists("sensitive_working2")) sensitive_working2 else if (exists("sensitive_working")) sensitive_working else sensitive
fin_E  <- if (exists("financial_working2")) financial_working2 else if (exists("financial_working_B")) financial_working_B else financial_comp

p1_E   <- p1_E   %>% dplyr::mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))
p2_E   <- p2_E   %>% dplyr::mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))
sens_E <- sens_E %>% dplyr::mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))
fin_E  <- fin_E  %>% dplyr::mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))

# Ensure financial has cleaned name for downstream evidence rebuild
if (!("fc_name_clean" %in% names(fin_E))) {
  fin_E <- fin_E %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      fc_name = as.character(fc_name),
      fc_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(stringr::str_to_title(fc_name)),
      fc_name_clean = clean_name(fc_name_title)
    )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Stage summary helper (rows, progress, finished, status) by ppn
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
summarise_stage_by_ppn <- function(df, stage_prefix) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(
      canonical_ppn = character(),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_n_rows") := integer(),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_progress_max") := numeric(),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_finished_any") := logical(),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_status") := character()
    ))
  }

  df <- df %>% dplyr::mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))

  has_progress <- "Progress" %in% names(df)
  has_finished <- "Finished" %in% names(df)

  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(ppn) & ppn != "") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(ppn) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_rows = dplyr::n(),
      progress_max = if (has_progress) suppressWarnings(max(as.numeric(Progress), na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_,
      finished_any = if (has_finished) any(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Finished)) == 1, na.rm = TRUE) else NA,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      stage_status = dplyr::case_when(
        n_rows == 0 ~ "missing",
        !is.na(finished_any) & finished_any ~ "complete",
        !is.na(progress_max) & progress_max >= 100 ~ "complete",
        TRUE ~ "partial"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      canonical_ppn = ppn,
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_n_rows") := as.integer(n_rows),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_progress_max") := as.numeric(progress_max),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_finished_any") := as.logical(finished_any),
      !!paste0(stage_prefix, "_status") := as.character(stage_status)
    )
}

# IC stage: ResponseId is canonical ppn
ic_stage <- ic_ledger_working %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ResponseId = trimws(as.character(ResponseId))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ResponseId) & ResponseId != "") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ResponseId) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(ic_n_rows = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    canonical_ppn = ResponseId,
    ic_n_rows = as.integer(ic_n_rows),
    ic_progress_max = as.numeric(NA),
    ic_finished_any = as.logical(NA),
    ic_status = "present"
  )

sens_stage  <- summarise_stage_by_ppn(sens_E, "sens")
part1_stage <- summarise_stage_by_ppn(p1_E,   "part1")
part2_stage <- summarise_stage_by_ppn(p2_E,   "part2")
fin_stage   <- summarise_stage_by_ppn(fin_E,  "fin")

stage_summary <- ic_stage %>%
  dplyr::full_join(sens_stage,  by = "canonical_ppn") %>%
  dplyr::full_join(part1_stage, by = "canonical_ppn") %>%
  dplyr::full_join(part2_stage, by = "canonical_ppn") %>%
  dplyr::full_join(fin_stage,   by = "canonical_ppn") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ic_n_rows    = ifelse(is.na(ic_n_rows), 0L, ic_n_rows),
    sens_n_rows  = ifelse(is.na(sens_n_rows), 0L, sens_n_rows),
    part1_n_rows = ifelse(is.na(part1_n_rows), 0L, part1_n_rows),
    part2_n_rows = ifelse(is.na(part2_n_rows), 0L, part2_n_rows),
    fin_n_rows   = ifelse(is.na(fin_n_rows), 0L, fin_n_rows),

    ic_status    = ifelse(is.na(ic_status) & ic_n_rows > 0, "present", ic_status),
    sens_status  = ifelse(is.na(sens_status)  & sens_n_rows  > 0, "partial", sens_status),
    part1_status = ifelse(is.na(part1_status) & part1_n_rows > 0, "partial", part1_status),
    part2_status = ifelse(is.na(part2_status) & part2_n_rows > 0, "partial", part2_status),
    fin_status   = ifelse(is.na(fin_status)   & fin_n_rows   > 0, "partial", fin_status),

    ic_status    = ifelse(is.na(ic_status), "missing", ic_status),
    sens_status  = ifelse(is.na(sens_status), "missing", sens_status),
    part1_status = ifelse(is.na(part1_status), "missing", part1_status),
    part2_status = ifelse(is.na(part2_status), "missing", part2_status),
    fin_status   = ifelse(is.na(fin_status), "missing", fin_status)
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Build ONE review table (ONLY canonical_score_auto < 7)
#    Use roster canonical_responseid_final as canonical ppn per identity.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
roster_ppn <- identity_roster %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    decision = ifelse(is.na(decision) | decision == "", "accept", as.character(decision)),
    canonical_responseid_final = trimws(as.character(canonical_responseid_final))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(decision != "drop") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Name_clean,
    canonical_ppn = canonical_responseid_final
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(canonical_ppn) & canonical_ppn != "") %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Name_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)

E_review_template <- identity_ledger %>%
  dplyr::left_join(roster_ppn, by = "Name_clean") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(canonical_ppn) & canonical_ppn != "") %>%
  dplyr::filter(canonical_score_auto < 7) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(stage_summary, by = "canonical_ppn") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    downstream_any_rows = (sens_n_rows + part1_n_rows + part2_n_rows + fin_n_rows) > 0L,
    keep = downstream_any_rows,
    drop_reason = dplyr::case_when(
      downstream_any_rows == FALSE ~ "ic_only_no_usable_downstream_data",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ),
    notes = ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Name_title,
    Name_clean,
    canonical_ppn,

    canonical_score_auto,
    max_score,
    review_priority,

    n_candidates_in_part1,
    n_candidates_in_part2,
    n_candidates_in_sens,
    n_candidates_in_fc_ppn,
    in_fc_by_name,

    scores_by_responseid,
    part1_by_responseid,
    part2_by_responseid,
    sens_by_responseid,

    ic_n_rows, ic_status,
    sens_n_rows, sens_progress_max, sens_finished_any, sens_status,
    part1_n_rows, part1_progress_max, part1_finished_any, part1_status,
    part2_n_rows, part2_progress_max, part2_finished_any, part2_status,
    fin_n_rows, fin_progress_max, fin_finished_any, fin_status,

    downstream_any_rows,

    keep, drop_reason, notes
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(canonical_score_auto, Name_title)

write_review_csv(E_review_template, "E_incompletes_review.csv")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Read decisions and compute drops
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
E_review <- read_audit_csv2("E_incompletes_review.csv") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Name_clean = as.character(Name_clean),
    canonical_ppn = trimws(as.character(canonical_ppn)),
    keep = as.logical(keep),
    drop_reason = as.character(drop_reason),
    notes = as.character(notes)
  )

stopifnot(nrow(E_review) == nrow(E_review_template))
stopifnot(all(E_review$Name_clean == E_review_template$Name_clean))
stopifnot(all(E_review$canonical_ppn == E_review_template$canonical_ppn))

drop_ppns_E <- E_review %>%
  dplyr::filter(keep == FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::pull(canonical_ppn) %>%
  unique()

drop_ppns_E <- drop_ppns_E[!is.na(drop_ppns_E) & drop_ppns_E != ""]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Apply drops only if needed, then rebuild identity_ledger and identity_roster
#    Also propagate the filtered datasets forward into the working objects that
#    later steps actually use.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_drop <- length(drop_ppns_E)

if (n_drop > 0) {

  ic_ledger_working <- ic_ledger_working %>%
    dplyr::mutate(ResponseId = trimws(as.character(ResponseId))) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!(ResponseId %in% drop_ppns_E))

  p1_E   <- p1_E   %>% dplyr::filter(!(ppn %in% drop_ppns_E))
  p2_E   <- p2_E   %>% dplyr::filter(!(ppn %in% drop_ppns_E))
  sens_E <- sens_E %>% dplyr::filter(!(ppn %in% drop_ppns_E))
  fin_E  <- fin_E  %>% dplyr::filter(!(ppn %in% drop_ppns_E))

  # Propagate Step E removals into the downstream working objects that later
  # steps use. This prevents dropped rows from re-entering in preF / F.
  part1_working2     <- p1_E
  part2_working2     <- p2_E
  sensitive_working2 <- sens_E
  financial_working2 <- fin_E

  part1_ppn_vec <- unique(part1_working2$ppn)
  part2_ppn_vec <- unique(part2_working2$ppn)
  sens_ppn_vec  <- unique(sensitive_working2$ppn)
  fin_ppn_vec   <- unique(financial_working2$ppn)

  ic_presence <- ic_ledger_working %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Name_clean, Name_title, ResponseId, flag_test_by_date, flag_test_by_name, StartDate_posix) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ResponseId = trimws(as.character(ResponseId)),
      in_part1   = ResponseId %in% part1_ppn_vec,
      in_part2   = ResponseId %in% part2_ppn_vec,
      in_sens    = ResponseId %in% sens_ppn_vec,
      in_fc_ppn  = ResponseId %in% fin_ppn_vec,
      in_fc_name = !is.na(Name_clean) & Name_clean != "" & (Name_clean %in% financial_working2$fc_name_clean)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      downstream_score =
        (in_part1 * 2L) +
        (in_part2 * 2L) +
        (in_sens  * 1L) +
        (in_fc_ppn * 1L) +
        (in_fc_name * 1L)
    )

  ic_ranked <- ic_presence %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Name_clean) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(downstream_score), StartDate_posix, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      n_ic_rows_for_name = dplyr::n(),
      canonical_responseid_auto = dplyr::first(ResponseId),
      canonical_score_auto = downstream_score[match(canonical_responseid_auto, ResponseId)],
      is_canonical_auto = ResponseId == canonical_responseid_auto
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4a) IC-based rebuilt identity ledger
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  identity_ledger_ic <- ic_ranked %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Name_clean) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      Name_title = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(Name_title)),
      n_ic_rows  = dplyr::first(n_ic_rows_for_name),

      canonical_responseid_auto = dplyr::first(canonical_responseid_auto),
      canonical_score_auto      = dplyr::first(canonical_score_auto),

      max_score = suppressWarnings(max(downstream_score, na.rm = TRUE)),
      n_at_max  = suppressWarnings(sum(downstream_score == max_score, na.rm = TRUE)),

      ic_start_min = suppressWarnings(min(StartDate_posix, na.rm = TRUE)),
      ic_start_max = suppressWarnings(max(StartDate_posix, na.rm = TRUE)),

      any_test_flags = any(flag_test_by_date | flag_test_by_name, na.rm = TRUE),

      n_candidates_in_part1  = sum(in_part1, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_candidates_in_part2  = sum(in_part2, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_candidates_in_sens   = sum(in_sens,  na.rm = TRUE),
      n_candidates_in_fc_ppn = sum(in_fc_ppn, na.rm = TRUE),
      in_fc_by_name          = any(in_fc_name, na.rm = TRUE),

      all_responseids = paste(ResponseId, collapse = " | "),
      scores_by_responseid = paste0(ResponseId, ":", downstream_score) %>% paste(collapse = " | "),
      part1_by_responseid  = paste0(ResponseId, ":", as.integer(in_part1)) %>% paste(collapse = " | "),
      part2_by_responseid  = paste0(ResponseId, ":", as.integer(in_part2)) %>% paste(collapse = " | "),
      sens_by_responseid   = paste0(ResponseId, ":", as.integer(in_sens))  %>% paste(collapse = " | "),

      reason_summary = dplyr::case_when(
        n_ic_rows == 1 ~ "single_ic_row",
        n_ic_rows > 1 & any(downstream_score > 0, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "multiple_ic_rows_pick_best_downstream",
        n_ic_rows > 1 ~ "multiple_ic_rows_no_downstream_signal",
        TRUE ~ "unknown"
      ),

      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ic_start_min = dplyr::if_else(is.infinite(ic_start_min), as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"), ic_start_min),
      ic_start_max = dplyr::if_else(is.infinite(ic_start_max), as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"), ic_start_max),

      flag_restart = n_ic_rows > 1,
      flag_tie_at_max = flag_restart & n_at_max > 1,
      flag_low_signal = canonical_score_auto == 0,

      auto_ok = canonical_score_auto >= 7 & !flag_tie_at_max & !any_test_flags,

      review_priority = dplyr::case_when(
        any_test_flags ~ "review_high_test",
        flag_tie_at_max ~ "review_high_tie",
        canonical_score_auto == 0 ~ "review_high_no_signal",
        canonical_score_auto < 7 ~ "review_medium_low_score",
        TRUE ~ "auto_ok"
      )
    )

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4b) Synthetic-only rebuilt identities from post-drop downstream data
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  synthetic_identity_ledger <- financial_working2 %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)),
      fc_name_title = as.character(fc_name_title),
      fc_name_clean = as.character(fc_name_clean)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(ppn),
      ppn != "",
      stringr::str_starts(ppn, synthetic_prefix),
      !is.na(fc_name_clean),
      fc_name_clean != ""
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(ppn, fc_name_clean, fc_name_title) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      in_part1   = ppn %in% part1_ppn_vec,
      in_part2   = ppn %in% part2_ppn_vec,
      in_sens    = ppn %in% sens_ppn_vec,
      in_fc_ppn  = ppn %in% fin_ppn_vec,
      in_fc_name = TRUE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      downstream_score =
        (in_part1 * 2L) +
        (in_part2 * 2L) +
        (in_sens  * 1L) +
        (in_fc_ppn * 1L) +
        (in_fc_name * 1L)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Name_clean = fc_name_clean,
      Name_title = fc_name_title,
      n_ic_rows  = 0L,

      canonical_responseid_auto = ppn,
      canonical_score_auto      = downstream_score,

      max_score = downstream_score,
      n_at_max  = 1L,

      ic_start_min = as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"),
      ic_start_max = as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC"),

      any_test_flags = FALSE,

      n_candidates_in_part1  = as.integer(in_part1),
      n_candidates_in_part2  = as.integer(in_part2),
      n_candidates_in_sens   = as.integer(in_sens),
      n_candidates_in_fc_ppn = as.integer(in_fc_ppn),
      in_fc_by_name          = TRUE,

      all_responseids = ppn,
      scores_by_responseid = paste0(ppn, ":", downstream_score),
      part1_by_responseid  = paste0(ppn, ":", as.integer(in_part1)),
      part2_by_responseid  = paste0(ppn, ":", as.integer(in_part2)),
      sens_by_responseid   = paste0(ppn, ":", as.integer(in_sens)),

      reason_summary = "synthetic_financial_only",

      flag_restart    = FALSE,
      flag_tie_at_max = FALSE,
      flag_low_signal = canonical_score_auto == 0,

      auto_ok = canonical_score_auto >= 7,

      review_priority = dplyr::case_when(
        canonical_score_auto == 0 ~ "review_high_no_signal",
        canonical_score_auto < 7 ~ "review_medium_low_score",
        TRUE ~ "auto_ok"
      )
    )

  # If an IC identity already exists for the same Name_clean, keep the IC identity
  synthetic_identity_ledger <- synthetic_identity_ledger %>%
    dplyr::filter(!(Name_clean %in% identity_ledger_ic$Name_clean))

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4c) Final rebuilt identity ledger
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  identity_ledger <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    identity_ledger_ic,
    synthetic_identity_ledger
  ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(review_priority, Name_title)

  # Preserve any existing manual restarter decisions already in identity_roster
  manual_decisions <- identity_roster %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Name_clean,
      decision_manual = as.character(decision),
      canonical_responseid_final_manual = as.character(canonical_responseid_final),
      drop_reason_manual = as.character(drop_reason),
      notes_manual = as.character(notes)
    )

  identity_roster <- identity_ledger %>%
    dplyr::left_join(manual_decisions, by = "Name_clean") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      decision = ifelse(!is.na(decision_manual) & decision_manual != "", decision_manual, "accept"),
      canonical_responseid_final = dplyr::case_when(
        decision == "override" &
          !is.na(canonical_responseid_final_manual) &
          canonical_responseid_final_manual != "" ~ canonical_responseid_final_manual,
        decision == "drop" ~ NA_character_,
        TRUE ~ canonical_responseid_auto
      ),
      drop_reason = ifelse(!is.na(drop_reason_manual) & drop_reason_manual != "", drop_reason_manual, ""),
      notes = ifelse(!is.na(notes_manual) & notes_manual != "", notes_manual, "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::ends_with("_manual"))

  identity_roster <- identity_roster %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      override_is_valid = ifelse(
        decision == "override" & !is.na(canonical_responseid_final) & canonical_responseid_final != "",
        stringr::str_detect(all_responseids, stringr::fixed(canonical_responseid_final)),
        TRUE
      )
    )
  stopifnot(all(identity_roster$override_is_valid))

} else {

  # Even if nothing is dropped, keep the object chain explicit so later steps
  # continue from the same current datasets rather than falling back to older ones.
  part1_working2     <- p1_E
  part2_working2     <- p2_E
  sensitive_working2 <- sens_E
  financial_working2 <- fin_E
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Single receipt (always) -> receipts_dir
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
E_receipt <- tibble::tibble(
  n_incompletes_in_review = nrow(E_review_template),
  n_marked_drop = n_drop,
  n_marked_keep = nrow(E_review_template) - n_drop
)

write_receipt_csv(E_receipt, "E_incompletes_receipt.csv")
```






```{r}
###############################################################################
# STEP preF) PURGE NON-CANONICAL / UNLINKABLE ROWS BEFORE LINKAGE
#
# Goal:
#   Remove downstream rows that still cannot receive a gutsID in Step F.
#
# Why this step is needed:
#   Earlier identity steps resolve restart clusters and select exactly one
#   canonical_responseid_final per identity. Step F propagates gutsID only
#   through canonical identities retained in identity_roster.
#
#   At this point, some downstream rows may still be unusable because they:
#     1) use a known non-canonical restart alias
#     2) contain a placeholder / malformed ppn value
#     3) have a ppn that does not belong to any surviving accepted identity
#
#   If those rows are left in place, they survive into Step F but cannot
#   receive a gutsID, which creates missing IDs in the final outputs.
#
# Strategy:
#   1) Select the most current downstream working datasets
#   2) Build an alias-level identity universe from surviving accepted identities
#   3) Flag ppns that are unusable for linkage
#   4) Purge those rows from Part1 / Part2 / Sensitive / Financial
#   5) Write one audit file and one compact receipt
#
# Outputs:
#   - One audit file:
#       preF_noncanonical_purge_review.csv
#   - One receipt file:
#       preF_noncanonical_purge_receipt.csv
#
# End result:
#   Only rows with linkage-eligible ppn values survive into Step F.
###############################################################################

stopifnot(exists("identity_roster"))
stopifnot(exists("write_audit_csv"))
stopifnot(exists("write_receipt_csv"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0) Select current downstream working datasets
# ------------------------------------------------------------
part1_src <- if (exists("part1_working2")) part1_working2 else if (exists("part1_working")) part1_working else part1
part2_src <- if (exists("part2_working2")) part2_working2 else if (exists("part2_working")) part2_working else part2
sens_src  <- if (exists("sensitive_working2")) sensitive_working2 else if (exists("sensitive_working")) sensitive_working else sensitive
fin_src   <- if (exists("financial_working2")) financial_working2 else if (exists("financial_working_B")) financial_working_B else financial_comp

stopifnot(exists("part1_src"))
stopifnot(exists("part2_src"))
stopifnot(exists("sens_src"))
stopifnot(exists("fin_src"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Local helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------
preF_is_missing_ppn <- function(x) {
  x2 <- trimws(as.character(x))
  is.na(x2) |
    x2 == "" |
    x2 %in% c("NA", "N/A", "NULL")
}

preF_is_placeholder_ppn <- function(x) {
  x2 <- trimws(as.character(x))
  !is.na(x2) & x2 != "" & (
    stringr::str_detect(x2, "^\\{e://Field/.*\\}$") |
    stringr::str_detect(x2, "^SYN_\\{e://Field/.*\\}") |
    stringr::str_detect(x2, "^\\{.*\\}$")
  )
}

preF_is_bad_ppn <- function(x) {
  preF_is_missing_ppn(x) | preF_is_placeholder_ppn(x)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Build accepted identity universe from identity_roster
# ------------------------------------------------------------
identity_roster_std <- identity_roster %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    decision = ifelse(is.na(decision) | decision == "", "accept", as.character(decision)),
    Name_title = as.character(Name_title),
    canonical_responseid_final = trimws(as.character(canonical_responseid_final)),
    all_responseids = as.character(all_responseids),
    drop_reason = ifelse(is.na(drop_reason), "", as.character(drop_reason)),
    notes = ifelse(is.na(notes), "", as.character(notes))
  )

# Identities that should survive into linkage
preF_identity_keep <- identity_roster_std %>%
  dplyr::filter(decision != "drop") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!preF_is_missing_ppn(canonical_responseid_final)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!preF_is_placeholder_ppn(canonical_responseid_final)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Name_title,
    canonical_ppn = canonical_responseid_final,
    drop_reason,
    notes
  )

# Alias-level map across all retained identities
preF_alias_map <- identity_roster_std %>%
  dplyr::filter(decision != "drop") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!preF_is_missing_ppn(canonical_responseid_final)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!preF_is_placeholder_ppn(canonical_responseid_final)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(alias_ppn = stringr::str_split(all_responseids, "\\s*\\|\\s*")) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(alias_ppn) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    alias_ppn = trimws(as.character(alias_ppn)),
    is_canonical = alias_ppn == canonical_responseid_final
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!preF_is_missing_ppn(alias_ppn)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!preF_is_placeholder_ppn(alias_ppn)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Name_title,
    canonical_ppn = canonical_responseid_final,
    alias_ppn,
    is_canonical
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

# Hard stop if one alias maps to more than one canonical identity
preF_alias_conflicts <- preF_alias_map %>%
  dplyr::group_by(alias_ppn) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_canonical = dplyr::n_distinct(canonical_ppn),
    canonical_ppn = paste(sort(unique(canonical_ppn)), collapse = " | "),
    Name_title = paste(sort(unique(Name_title)), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_canonical > 1)

stopifnot(nrow(preF_alias_conflicts) == 0)

# Known noncanonical aliases that should be removed
preF_noncanonical_aliases <- preF_alias_map %>%
  dplyr::filter(is_canonical == FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(alias_ppn, canonical_ppn, Name_title)

# Valid linkage ppn universe after all prior identity decisions
preF_valid_ppns <- preF_alias_map %>%
  dplyr::distinct(alias_ppn) %>%
  dplyr::pull(alias_ppn)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Helper to classify and purge unusable rows
# ------------------------------------------------------------
purge_preF_rows <- function(df, dataset_name, alias_tbl, valid_ppns) {

  df_std <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn))
    )

  dropped <- df_std %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dataset = dataset_name,
      issue_type = dplyr::case_when(
        preF_is_missing_ppn(ppn) ~ "missing_ppn_purged",
        preF_is_placeholder_ppn(ppn) ~ "placeholder_or_malformed_ppn_purged",
        ppn %in% alias_tbl$alias_ppn ~ "noncanonical_restart_ppn_purged",
        !(ppn %in% valid_ppns) ~ "no_surviving_identity_match_purged",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(issue_type)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      alias_tbl,
      by = c("ppn" = "alias_ppn")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      details = dplyr::case_when(
        issue_type == "noncanonical_restart_ppn_purged" ~ paste0("canonical_ppn=", canonical_ppn),
        issue_type == "missing_ppn_purged" ~ "ppn missing after prior repair steps",
        issue_type == "placeholder_or_malformed_ppn_purged" ~ "ppn is placeholder or malformed value",
        issue_type == "no_surviving_identity_match_purged" ~ "ppn not found in accepted identity_roster universe",
        TRUE ~ ""
      )
    )

  kept <- df_std %>%
    dplyr::filter(!(ppn %in% dropped$ppn & dplyr::row_number() %in% match(seq_len(nrow(df_std)), seq_len(nrow(df_std)))) )

  # Simpler / safer keep logic: remove exact dropped rows by temporary row id
  df_tagged <- df_std %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.pref_row_id = dplyr::row_number())

  dropped <- df_tagged %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dataset = dataset_name,
      issue_type = dplyr::case_when(
        preF_is_missing_ppn(ppn) ~ "missing_ppn_purged",
        preF_is_placeholder_ppn(ppn) ~ "placeholder_or_malformed_ppn_purged",
        ppn %in% alias_tbl$alias_ppn ~ "noncanonical_restart_ppn_purged",
        !(ppn %in% valid_ppns) ~ "no_surviving_identity_match_purged",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(issue_type)) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      alias_tbl,
      by = c("ppn" = "alias_ppn")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      details = dplyr::case_when(
        issue_type == "noncanonical_restart_ppn_purged" ~ paste0("canonical_ppn=", canonical_ppn),
        issue_type == "missing_ppn_purged" ~ "ppn missing after prior repair steps",
        issue_type == "placeholder_or_malformed_ppn_purged" ~ "ppn is placeholder or malformed value",
        issue_type == "no_surviving_identity_match_purged" ~ "ppn not found in accepted identity_roster universe",
        TRUE ~ ""
      )
    )

  kept <- df_tagged %>%
    dplyr::filter(!(.pref_row_id %in% dropped$.pref_row_id)) %>%
    dplyr::select(-.pref_row_id)

  dropped <- dropped %>%
    dplyr::select(-.pref_row_id)

  list(
    kept = kept,
    dropped = dropped
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Apply purge to each downstream dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------
part1_preF <- purge_preF_rows(part1_src, "part1", preF_noncanonical_aliases, preF_valid_ppns)
part2_preF <- purge_preF_rows(part2_src, "part2", preF_noncanonical_aliases, preF_valid_ppns)
sens_preF  <- purge_preF_rows(sens_src,  "sensitive", preF_noncanonical_aliases, preF_valid_ppns)
fin_preF   <- purge_preF_rows(fin_src,   "financial", preF_noncanonical_aliases, preF_valid_ppns)

# These are the objects Step F will preferentially use
part1_working3     <- part1_preF$kept
part2_working3     <- part2_preF$kept
sensitive_working3 <- sens_preF$kept
financial_working3 <- fin_preF$kept

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) One audit file
# ------------------------------------------------------------
preF_review <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  part1_preF$dropped,
  part2_preF$dropped,
  sens_preF$dropped,
  fin_preF$dropped
) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    issue_type,
    dataset,
    Name_title,
    ppn,
    canonical_ppn,
    details,
    everything()
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dataset, issue_type, Name_title, ppn)

write_audit_csv(preF_review, "preF_noncanonical_purge_review.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) One receipt file
# ------------------------------------------------------------
preF_receipt <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c(
    "n_valid_identity_ppns",
    "n_noncanonical_alias_ppn",
    "n_part1_rows_dropped",
    "n_part2_rows_dropped",
    "n_sensitive_rows_dropped",
    "n_financial_rows_dropped",
    "n_total_rows_dropped",
    "n_part1_rows_remaining",
    "n_part2_rows_remaining",
    "n_sensitive_rows_remaining",
    "n_financial_rows_remaining"
  ),
  value = c(
    length(preF_valid_ppns),
    nrow(preF_noncanonical_aliases),
    nrow(part1_preF$dropped),
    nrow(part2_preF$dropped),
    nrow(sens_preF$dropped),
    nrow(fin_preF$dropped),
    nrow(preF_review),
    nrow(part1_working3),
    nrow(part2_working3),
    nrow(sensitive_working3),
    nrow(financial_working3)
  )
)

write_receipt_csv(preF_receipt, "preF_noncanonical_purge_receipt.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) Sanity checks
# ------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(
  !any(trimws(as.character(part1_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_noncanonical_aliases$alias_ppn),
  !any(trimws(as.character(part2_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_noncanonical_aliases$alias_ppn),
  !any(trimws(as.character(sensitive_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_noncanonical_aliases$alias_ppn),
  !any(trimws(as.character(financial_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_noncanonical_aliases$alias_ppn)
)

stopifnot(
  !any(preF_is_bad_ppn(part1_working3$ppn)),
  !any(preF_is_bad_ppn(part2_working3$ppn)),
  !any(preF_is_bad_ppn(sensitive_working3$ppn)),
  !any(preF_is_bad_ppn(financial_working3$ppn))
)

stopifnot(
  all(trimws(as.character(part1_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_valid_ppns),
  all(trimws(as.character(part2_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_valid_ppns),
  all(trimws(as.character(sensitive_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_valid_ppns),
  all(trimws(as.character(financial_working3$ppn)) %in% preF_valid_ppns)
)

```


Linkage Step: Attach gutsID to the Canonical PPN and Propagate to All Survey Parts

This step connects the cleaned survey data to the consortium master identifier (gutsID) using the linkage file. At this point in the pipeline, we have:

A cleaned and optionally filtered IC ledger (ic_ledger_final) where ResponseId functions as the wave’s canonical participant identifier (the canonical ppn)

Downstream survey parts (sensitive_final, part1_final, part2_final, financial_final) that now have maximally complete ppn columns

A formal identity resolution outcome already applied (restarts handled, shared link collisions handled, incompletes optionally removed)



Because the linkage file maps participant names to gutsID, and IC is the only stage that reliably ties names to canonical ResponseId, we perform the join in two phases:

Name normalization and matching (linkage ↔ IC)

Build a standardized name representation on both sides (Name_title, Name_title_key)

Join on Name_title_key to assign each IC row a gutsID

Export an audit table of IC names that do not appear in linkage, and optionally flag duplicate linkage keys that could cause one to many joins



Propagation (IC ResponseId ↔ downstream ppn)

Build a ResponseId → gutsID map from the joined IC ledger

Propagate gutsID to every downstream dataset by joining on ppn

Run a conflict check to ensure no canonical ResponseId maps to multiple gutsID values



The output of this step is the same set of *_final datasets, now augmented with a gutsID column that enables cross wave integration and clean merges with consortium level data.



```{r}
# AUDIT STEP F: LINKAGE (Identity Roster Name -> gutsID) AND PROPAGATION
###############################################################################
# Goal:
#   Attach the consortium identifier (gutsID) to each participant and propagate
#   it across all survey components using the identity roster.
#
# Core logic:
#   Earlier identity steps already resolved duplicate / restarting ResponseIds
#   and selected exactly one canonical_responseid_final per identity.
#
#   Step F therefore only needs two fields from identity_roster:
#     1) Name_title                  -> used to connect participant to linkage
#     2) canonical_responseid_final  -> used as ppn for downstream propagation
#
# Strategy:
#   1) Select the most current downstream datasets, preferring post-preF purge
#      objects (*_working3) when available
#   2) Standardize names in identity_roster and linkage into a stable key
#   3) Join identity_roster -> linkage to assign gutsID
#   4) Build canonical ppn -> gutsID map from identity_roster
#   5) Propagate gutsID to Sensitive / Part1 / Part2 / Financial using ppn
#
# Outputs:
#   - One audit review file:
#       F_linkage_review.csv
#   - One receipt file:
#       F_linkage_receipt.csv
#
# End result:
#   The script produces *_final objects containing gutsID and ppn for all parts.
###############################################################################

stopifnot(exists("linkage"))
stopifnot(exists("identity_roster"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0) Select current downstream working datasets
#    Prefer post-preF objects so canonical purge actually
#    propagates into the final linkage/export stage.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
part1_src <- if (exists("part1_working3")) {
  part1_working3
} else if (exists("part1_working2")) {
  part1_working2
} else if (exists("part1_working")) {
  part1_working
} else {
  part1
}

part2_src <- if (exists("part2_working3")) {
  part2_working3
} else if (exists("part2_working2")) {
  part2_working2
} else if (exists("part2_working")) {
  part2_working
} else {
  part2
}

sens_src <- if (exists("sensitive_working3")) {
  sensitive_working3
} else if (exists("sensitive_working2")) {
  sensitive_working2
} else if (exists("sensitive_working")) {
  sensitive_working
} else {
  sensitive
}

fin_src <- if (exists("financial_working3")) {
  financial_working3
} else if (exists("financial_working2")) {
  financial_working2
} else if (exists("financial_working_B")) {
  financial_working_B
} else {
  financial_comp
}

stopifnot(exists("part1_src"))
stopifnot(exists("part2_src"))
stopifnot(exists("sens_src"))
stopifnot(exists("fin_src"))

part1_src <- part1_src %>%
  mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))

part2_src <- part2_src %>%
  mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))

sens_src <- sens_src %>%
  mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))

fin_src <- fin_src %>%
  mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn)))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Standardize roster names before linkage matching.
#
# Participant-specific corrections should be handled in the secure audit trail
# or a private configuration file, not hard-coded in the public repository.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
roster_fixed <- identity_roster %>%
  mutate(
    Name_title = as.character(Name_title)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Build stable title key used for joining roster <-> linkage
# ------------------------------------------------------------
make_title_key <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    as.character() %>%
    stringr::str_squish() %>%
    stringi::stri_trans_nfc() %>%
    stringr::str_to_title() %>%
    fix_tussenvoegsels()
}

linkage_key <- linkage %>%
  mutate(
    Name = as.character(Name),
    Name_title = make_title_key(Name),
    Name_title_key = clean_name(Name_title)
  ) %>%
  select(gutsID = ID, Name, Name_title, Name_title_key) %>%
  distinct()

roster_key <- roster_fixed %>%
  mutate(
    Name_title = make_title_key(Name_title),
    Name_title_key = clean_name(Name_title),
    canonical_responseid_final = trimws(as.character(canonical_responseid_final)),
    decision = ifelse(is.na(decision) | decision == "", "accept", as.character(decision))
  ) %>%
  filter(decision != "drop") %>%
  filter(!is.na(canonical_responseid_final) & canonical_responseid_final != "") %>%
  distinct()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Join identity_roster -> linkage to assign gutsID
# ------------------------------------------------------------
roster_linked <- roster_key %>%
  left_join(
    linkage_key %>% select(gutsID, Name_title_key),
    by = "Name_title_key"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Audit checks
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# A) Roster names that do not exist in linkage
roster_to_linkage_status <- roster_key %>%
  left_join(
    linkage_key %>% transmute(Name_title_key, in_linkage = TRUE),
    by = "Name_title_key"
  ) %>%
  mutate(in_linkage = !is.na(in_linkage))

roster_unmatched <- roster_to_linkage_status %>%
  filter(in_linkage == FALSE) %>%
  transmute(
    issue_type = "roster_name_missing_in_linkage",
    Name_title = Name_title,
    Name_title_key = Name_title_key,
    canonical_ppn = canonical_responseid_final,
    gutsID = NA_character_,
    details = ""
  )

# B) Linkage duplicate keys
linkage_dupes <- linkage_key %>%
  count(Name_title_key, Name_title, sort = TRUE) %>%
  filter(n > 1) %>%
  transmute(
    issue_type = "linkage_duplicate_name_key",
    Name_title = Name_title,
    Name_title_key = Name_title_key,
    canonical_ppn = NA_character_,
    gutsID = NA_character_,
    details = paste0("n_rows=", n)
  )

# C) Canonical ppns mapping to multiple gutsIDs
canonical_gutsid_conflicts <- roster_linked %>%
  filter(!is.na(canonical_responseid_final) & canonical_responseid_final != "") %>%
  group_by(canonical_responseid_final) %>%
  summarise(
    n_gutsIDs = n_distinct(na.omit(gutsID)),
    gutsIDs = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(gutsID))), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_gutsIDs > 1) %>%
  transmute(
    issue_type = "canonical_ppn_maps_to_multiple_gutsid",
    Name_title = NA_character_,
    Name_title_key = NA_character_,
    canonical_ppn = canonical_responseid_final,
    gutsID = NA_character_,
    details = paste0("gutsIDs=", gutsIDs)
  )

F_review <- bind_rows(
  roster_unmatched,
  linkage_dupes,
  canonical_gutsid_conflicts
)

write_audit_csv(F_review, "F_linkage_review.csv")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) Build canonical ppn -> gutsID map
# ------------------------------------------------------------
ppn_to_gutsid <- roster_linked %>%
  transmute(
    ppn = canonical_responseid_final,
    gutsID = as.character(gutsID)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ppn) & ppn != "") %>%
  distinct(ppn, .keep_all = TRUE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Propagate gutsID to all downstream datasets
# ------------------------------------------------------------
add_gutsid <- function(df, map_tbl) {
  df %>%
    mutate(ppn = trimws(as.character(ppn))) %>%
    left_join(map_tbl, by = "ppn")
}

part1_linked <- add_gutsid(part1_src, ppn_to_gutsid)
part2_linked <- add_gutsid(part2_src, ppn_to_gutsid)
sens_linked  <- add_gutsid(sens_src,  ppn_to_gutsid)
fin_linked   <- add_gutsid(fin_src,   ppn_to_gutsid)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) Final outputs
# ------------------------------------------------------------
identity_roster_final <- roster_linked
part1_final           <- part1_linked
part2_final           <- part2_linked
sensitive_final       <- sens_linked
financial_final       <- fin_linked

move_gutsid_first <- function(df) {
  if (!"gutsID" %in% names(df)) return(df)
  df %>% dplyr::select(gutsID, dplyr::everything())
}

identity_roster_final <- move_gutsid_first(identity_roster_final)
part1_final           <- move_gutsid_first(part1_final)
part2_final           <- move_gutsid_first(part2_final)
sensitive_final       <- move_gutsid_first(sensitive_final)
financial_final       <- move_gutsid_first(financial_final)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8) Receipt summary
# ------------------------------------------------------------
F_receipt <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c(
    "n_identity_roster_rows_used",
    "n_ppn_to_gutsid_rows",
    "n_part1_rows",
    "n_part2_rows",
    "n_sensitive_rows",
    "n_financial_rows",
    "n_part1_missing_gutsid",
    "n_part2_missing_gutsid",
    "n_sensitive_missing_gutsid",
    "n_financial_missing_gutsid"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(identity_roster_final),
    nrow(ppn_to_gutsid),
    nrow(part1_final),
    nrow(part2_final),
    nrow(sensitive_final),
    nrow(financial_final),
    sum(is.na(part1_final$gutsID) | part1_final$gutsID == ""),
    sum(is.na(part2_final$gutsID) | part2_final$gutsID == ""),
    sum(is.na(sensitive_final$gutsID) | sensitive_final$gutsID == ""),
    sum(is.na(financial_final$gutsID) | financial_final$gutsID == "")
  )
)

write_receipt_csv(F_receipt, "F_linkage_receipt.csv")

```


Sociometrics Cleaning Overview Comments

Purpose

This stage cleans and anonymizes the sociometric nomination columns in Part 2. In these columns, identifiable nominee names are often stored in metadata, especially the variable label (and occasionally value labels). To support sharing and analysis, any name-bearing metadata must be replaced with a stable anonymous identifier (gutsID) while preserving the underlying response values.



What makes sociometrics different

Unlike most survey fields where meaning is contained in the cell values, sociometric columns often behave like “one column per nominee,” where:

The column name indicates which sociometric question group it belongs to (q-group / prefix pattern).

The variable label contains the nominee’s name.

The cell values contain the nomination outcome or tie strength.

As a result, the primary cleaning task here is metadata anonymization, not value transformation.



Inputs required

This step assumes the linkage stage has already produced:

part2_final (Part 2 after identity repairs; may already include gutsID for respondents)

linkage (master table containing gutsID and participant names)

It also assumes the standard name normalization helpers are available (fix_tussenvoegsels(), clean_name()), so nominee names are mapped using the same conventions as the rest of the pipeline.



High-level strategy

This is a review-driven anonymization pipeline:

Identify sociometric columns in part2_final using a prefix-based rule plus explicit exclusions.

Extract a nominee name from each column’s variable label using a robust parsing approach designed to tolerate inconsistent label formatting.

Map nominee name → gutsID using linkage:

Exact match when possible (based on normalized name keys)

Fuzzy suggestions when exact match fails (review-only; never applied automatically)

Write one review file containing only the cases needing human attention (parse failures, unmatched names, or fuzzy candidates).



Read the edited review file and apply decisions:

keep_final determines whether a column is kept and anonymized

gutsID_override allows a manual correction of the mapping

name_override allows a manual correction of the parsed nominee name (and triggers a re-check for an exact match)



Anonymize only the kept columns by:

removing value labels so no names persist there

replacing the variable label with the mapped gutsID

This keeps the raw values intact while removing name-bearing metadata from the columns that will be used.



Conservative defaults

This step is intentionally conservative:

Exact matches are auto-kept and anonymized.

Any non-exact (fuzzy/unmatched/parse-failed) case is not anonymized unless explicitly approved via keep_final and a valid gutsID (either suggested or overridden).

Columns that are not kept remain present in part2_final but retain their original labels and should be treated as not safe for downstream use unless later approved and reprocessed.



Outputs

This stage produces:

One review audit file (editable)
S2_sociometric_mapping_review.csv
Contains only columns requiring review (parse failures / unmatched / fuzzy suggestions), along with evidence and editable fields (keep_final, gutsID_override, name_override).

One receipt (non-editable, written to receipts folder)
S_receipt_sociometrics.csv
A compact summary of how many sociometric columns were detected, how many were anonymized, and how many were left unanonymized.



End result

By the end of this stage:

part2_final contains a subset of sociometric columns whose variable labels are gutsIDs, not names

those anonymized columns have value labels removed

any sociometric columns that were not approved or could not be mapped remain explicitly documented in S2 and remain unanonymized unless manually approved and rerun through this step



```{r}
###############################################################################
# SOCIOMETRICS CLEANING (Part 2 only)
#
# Goal:
#   - Identify sociometric nomination columns in part2_final
#   - Extract nominee name from each column's VARIABLE LABEL (robust parsing)
#   - Map nominee name -> gutsID via linkage (exact + fuzzy suggestions)
#   - Write REVIEW-ONLY audit CSV (parse failures / unmatched / fuzzy)
#   - Read edited audit CSV and apply:
#       - keep_final controls whether a column is treated as confidently mapped
#       - gutsID_override can override any suggested ID
#       - name_override can correct parsed nominee name (informational)
#
# PATCH (critical):
#   Always sanitize ALL sociometric columns so NO identifying info persists,
#   even when a name does not match or review is incomplete.
#     - remove ALL value labels on every sociometric column
#     - overwrite var_label on every sociometric column:
#         * if kept + mapped: var_label = gutsID_final
#         * else: var_label = safe placeholder (or blank), NEVER original text
#   By default, DO NOT drop any sociometric columns (no data purge).
###############################################################################

stopifnot(exists("part2_final"))
stopifnot(exists("linkage"))
stopifnot(exists("write_audit_csv"))
stopifnot(exists("read_audit_csv2"))
stopifnot(exists("fix_tussenvoegsels"))
stopifnot(exists("clean_name"))

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(tibble)
  library(labelled)
  library(sjmisc)
  library(stringdist)
})

# -------------------------
# Controls
# -------------------------
soc_prefix <- "sociometric"

# Exclusions: sociometric items that are NOT nominations (open questions etc.)
exclude_regex <- c(
  "sociometric_q_?(0?8)($|_)",
  "sociometric_q_?(2[2-4])($|_)",
  "^sociometric_q_?21$"
)

# Optional participant-specific parsing corrections.
# Define these only in the private config as a named character vector whose
# names are exact sociometric column names and whose values are corrected
# nominee names. Do not commit identifying values to the repository.
if (!exists("sociometric_name_patches", inherits = FALSE)) {
  sociometric_name_patches <- character(0)
}

# Fuzzy settings
fuzzy_method    <- "jw"
fuzzy_top_k     <- 5
fuzzy_ambig_eps <- 0.005

# Review outputs
review_csv <- "S2_sociometric_mapping_review.csv"

# PATCH behavior controls
drop_unmapped_sociometrics <- FALSE  # IMPORTANT: default FALSE to prevent purge
use_blank_placeholder <- FALSE       # if TRUE, unmapped labels become "" instead of UNMAPPED|...

# -------------------------
# Helpers
# -------------------------
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0 || is.na(a)) b else a

.is_plausible_name <- function(x) {
  x <- str_squish(as.character(x))
  if (is.na(x) || x == "") return(FALSE)
  if (nchar(x) < 3 || nchar(x) > 80) return(FALSE)
  if (str_detect(x, "[0-9]")) return(FALSE)
  if (str_detect(x, "[\\?\\!\\:;\\=\\+\\|]")) return(FALSE)
  if (str_detect(x, "\\bwww\\b|\\bhttp\\b")) return(FALSE)
  if (!str_detect(x, "[[:alpha:]]")) return(FALSE)
  TRUE
}

.score_name_candidate <- function(x) {
  x <- str_squish(as.character(x))
  if (!.is_plausible_name(x)) return(-Inf)

  # discourage question-like starters
  if (str_detect(str_to_lower(x), "^(wie|wat|waar|wanneer|waarom|welke|hoe)\\b")) return(-Inf)

  toks <- unlist(str_split(x, "\\s+"))
  ntok <- length(toks)
  if (ntok < 1 || ntok > 6) return(-Inf)

  name_token_ok <- function(t) {
    t_low <- str_to_lower(t)
    if (t_low %in% c("van","de","der","den","ter","ten","het","'t","le","la","du","da","di","dos","das","del","della")) return(TRUE)
    str_detect(t, "^[[:alpha:]][[:alpha:]'’\\-]+$") || str_detect(t, "^[[:alpha:]]+$")
  }
  if (!all(vapply(toks, name_token_ok, logical(1)))) return(-Inf)

  score <- 0
  score <- score + ifelse(ntok %in% 2:4, 3, ifelse(ntok == 1, 1, 0))
  if (any(str_to_lower(toks) %in% c("van","de","der","den","ter","ten","'t","het"))) score <- score + 1
  if (str_detect(x, "[\\,\\(\\)\\[\\]\\{\\}]")) score <- score - 1
  score <- score + max(0, 1 - (nchar(x) / 100))
  score
}

.clean_candidate <- function(x) {
  x <- str_squish(as.character(x))
  x <- str_replace_all(x, "^[\\s\"'“”‘’\\(\\[\\{\\-\\–\\—\\.:]+", "")
  x <- str_replace_all(x, "[\\s\"'“”‘’\\)\\]\\}\\-\\–\\—\\.:]+$", "")
  str_squish(x)
}

.after_last <- function(text, pattern) {
  m <- str_locate_all(text, pattern)[[1]]
  if (nrow(m) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  start <- m[nrow(m), 2] + 1
  substr(text, start, nchar(text))
}

extract_nominee_name <- function(colname, raw_label) {
  raw_label <- str_squish(as.character(raw_label %||% ""))
  if (raw_label == "NA") raw_label <- ""

  # Apply an optional correction supplied through the private config.
  if (length(sociometric_name_patches) > 0 &&
      colname %in% names(sociometric_name_patches)) {
    return(unname(sociometric_name_patches[[colname]]))
  }

  cands <- c(
    .after_last(raw_label, "\\?\\s+"),
    .after_last(raw_label, "\\s\\-\\s+"),
    .after_last(raw_label, "\\-\\s+"),
    .after_last(raw_label, "\\.\\s+"),
    .after_last(raw_label, "\\)\\s+")
  )

  cands <- vapply(cands, .clean_candidate, character(1))
  cands[cands == "" | is.na(cands)] <- NA_character_
  cands[cands == raw_label] <- NA_character_

  if (all(is.na(cands))) return("")

  scores <- vapply(cands, .score_name_candidate, numeric(1))
  if (all(!is.finite(scores))) {
    c_non <- cands[!is.na(cands)]
    return(c_non[which.min(nchar(c_non))])
  }

  cands[which.max(scores)]
}

safe_placeholder_label <- function(cn, q_group = NA_character_, blank = FALSE) {
  if (blank) return("")
  if (!is.na(q_group) && q_group != "") return(paste0("UNMAPPED|", q_group, "|", cn))
  paste0("UNMAPPED|", cn)
}

# -------------------------
# Linkage lookup
# -------------------------
linkage_key <- linkage %>%
  mutate(
    Name = as.character(Name),
    Name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(str_to_title(str_squish(Name))),
    Name_clean = clean_name(Name_title),
    gutsID = as.character(ID)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gutsID) & gutsID != "", !is.na(Name_clean) & Name_clean != "") %>%
  distinct(Name_clean, gutsID, Name_title)

linkage_first <- linkage_key %>%
  group_by(Name_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    gutsID_exact = first(gutsID),
    linkage_name_title_exact = first(Name_title),
    n_ids_for_name = n_distinct(gutsID),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

linkage_names_clean <- linkage_key$Name_clean
linkage_names_title <- linkage_key$Name_title
linkage_ids         <- linkage_key$gutsID

# -------------------------
# Sociometric columns (candidates)
# -------------------------
soc_cols <- grep(soc_prefix, names(part2_final), value = TRUE)
for (rx in exclude_regex) soc_cols <- soc_cols[!grepl(rx, soc_cols)]
message("Sociometric columns detected (post-exclusions): ", length(soc_cols))

# -------------------------
# Parse variable labels -> nominee name
# -------------------------
soc_parse <- tibble(
  colname = soc_cols,
  raw_label = vapply(soc_cols, function(cn) {
    lb <- labelled::var_label(part2_final[[cn]])
    if (is.null(lb) || is.na(lb)) "" else as.character(lb)
  }, character(1))
) %>%
  mutate(
    extracted_name = vapply(seq_along(colname), function(i) extract_nominee_name(colname[i], raw_label[i]), character(1)),
    nominee_name_title = fix_tussenvoegsels(str_to_title(str_squish(extracted_name))),
    nominee_name_clean = clean_name(nominee_name_title),
    q_group = str_extract(colname, "sociometric_q\\d+")
  )

# -------------------------
# Exact mapping (by clean name)
# -------------------------
soc_exact <- soc_parse %>%
  left_join(linkage_first, by = c("nominee_name_clean" = "Name_clean")) %>%
  mutate(
    has_name = !is.na(nominee_name_clean) & nominee_name_clean != "",
    exact_hit = !is.na(gutsID_exact) & gutsID_exact != "",
    mapping_status = case_when(
      !has_name ~ "parse_failed",
      exact_hit ~ "exact",
      TRUE ~ "unmatched"
    )
  )

# -------------------------
# Fuzzy suggestions (ranked, deterministic)
# -------------------------
fuzzy_match_one <- function(name_clean) {
  if (is.na(name_clean) || name_clean == "") {
    return(list(best_dist = NA_real_, best_idx = NA_integer_, top_idx = integer(0), top_dist = numeric(0), ambiguous = FALSE))
  }

  d <- stringdist::stringdist(name_clean, linkage_names_clean, method = fuzzy_method)

  ord <- order(d, linkage_names_title, na.last = TRUE)
  ord <- ord[seq_len(min(length(ord), fuzzy_top_k))]

  top_idx  <- ord
  top_dist <- d[top_idx]

  ambiguous <- length(top_dist) >= 2 && abs(top_dist[2] - top_dist[1]) < fuzzy_ambig_eps

  list(
    best_dist = top_dist[1],
    best_idx = top_idx[1],
    top_idx = top_idx,
    top_dist = top_dist,
    ambiguous = ambiguous
  )
}

fuzzy_info <- lapply(soc_exact$nominee_name_clean, fuzzy_match_one)

soc_mapping_full <- soc_exact %>%
  mutate(
    best_dist = vapply(fuzzy_info, function(x) x$best_dist, numeric(1)),
    best_fuzzy_name = vapply(fuzzy_info, function(x) {
      if (is.na(x$best_idx)) "" else linkage_names_title[x$best_idx]
    }, character(1)),
    best_fuzzy_id = vapply(fuzzy_info, function(x) {
      if (is.na(x$best_idx)) "" else linkage_ids[x$best_idx]
    }, character(1)),
    best_is_ambiguous = vapply(fuzzy_info, function(x) isTRUE(x$ambiguous), logical(1)),
    fuzzy_candidates_all = vapply(fuzzy_info, function(x) {
      if (!length(x$top_idx)) return("")
      paste0(linkage_names_title[x$top_idx], " (", sprintf("%.3f", x$top_dist), ")", collapse = " | ")
    }, character(1)),
    fuzzy_candidate_ids_all = vapply(fuzzy_info, function(x) {
      if (!length(x$top_idx)) return("")
      paste(linkage_ids[x$top_idx], collapse = " | ")
    }, character(1)),
    keep_auto = FALSE,        # conservative: never auto keep fuzzy
    keep_final = NA,          # editable
    gutsID_override = "",     # editable
    name_override = ""        # editable
  )

# -------------------------
# Diagnostics: "used exact" checks (informational)
# -------------------------
exact_used_lookup <- soc_mapping_full %>%
  filter(mapping_status == "exact", !is.na(gutsID_exact), gutsID_exact != "") %>%
  group_by(gutsID_exact) %>%
  summarise(
    exact_cols_using_id = paste(unique(colname), collapse = " | "),
    exact_names_using_id = paste(unique(nominee_name_title), collapse = " | "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

soc_mapping_full <- soc_mapping_full %>%
  left_join(exact_used_lookup, by = c("best_fuzzy_id" = "gutsID_exact")) %>%
  mutate(
    exact_cols_using_id = ifelse(is.na(exact_cols_using_id), "", exact_cols_using_id),
    exact_names_using_id = ifelse(is.na(exact_names_using_id), "", exact_names_using_id),
    used_exact_anywhere = best_fuzzy_id != "" & exact_cols_using_id != ""
  )

soc_mapping_full <- soc_mapping_full %>%
  group_by(q_group) %>%
  mutate(
    exact_ids_in_group = list(unique(gutsID_exact[mapping_status == "exact" & !is.na(gutsID_exact) & gutsID_exact != ""])),
    used_exact_in_group = best_fuzzy_id != "" & best_fuzzy_id %in% exact_ids_in_group[[1]]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-exact_ids_in_group)

# -------------------------
# Write REVIEW-ONLY CSV (exclude clean exact matches)
# -------------------------
soc_review <- soc_mapping_full %>%
  filter(mapping_status != "exact") %>%
  transmute(
    colname,
    raw_label,
    extracted_name,
    nominee_name_clean,
    mapping_status,
    gutsID_exact,
    best_dist,
    best_fuzzy_name,
    best_fuzzy_id,
    best_is_ambiguous,
    fuzzy_candidates_all,
    fuzzy_candidate_ids_all,
    used_exact_in_group,
    used_exact_anywhere,
    exact_cols_using_id,
    exact_names_using_id,
    keep_auto,
    keep_final,        # EDITABLE: TRUE/FALSE
    gutsID_override,   # EDITABLE
    name_override      # EDITABLE
  ) %>%
  arrange(mapping_status, best_dist, best_is_ambiguous, colname)

write_review_csv(soc_review, review_csv)

message("Total sociometric cols considered: ", nrow(soc_mapping_full))
message("Exact (auto handled, excluded from review CSV): ", sum(soc_mapping_full$mapping_status == "exact", na.rm = TRUE))
message("Needs review (written to S2): ", nrow(soc_review))




# -------------------------
# Read edited review CSV + merge edits back
# Conservative defaults:
#   - If keep_final is blank, treat as FALSE
#   - gutsID_override wins if provided
#   - exact mappings are always kept
# -------------------------
review_edits <- read_audit_csv2(review_csv) %>%
  mutate(
    colname = as.character(colname),
    keep_final_raw = str_to_lower(str_squish(as.character(keep_final))),
    keep_final = case_when(
      keep_final_raw %in% c("true","t","1","yes","y") ~ TRUE,
      keep_final_raw %in% c("false","f","0","no","n") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    ),
    gutsID_override = str_squish(as.character(gutsID_override)),
    name_override   = str_squish(as.character(name_override))
  ) %>%
  select(colname, keep_final, gutsID_override, name_override)

soc_mapping_final <- soc_mapping_full %>%
  left_join(review_edits, by = "colname", suffix = c("", "_edit")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Use EDITED overrides (the *_edit columns), not the originals
    extracted_name_final = ifelse(!is.na(name_override_edit) & name_override_edit != "",
                                  name_override_edit, extracted_name),

    nominee_name_title_final = fix_tussenvoegsels(str_to_title(str_squish(extracted_name_final))),
    nominee_name_clean_final = clean_name(nominee_name_title_final),

    gutsID_exact_final = linkage_first$gutsID_exact[match(nominee_name_clean_final, linkage_first$Name_clean)],
    mapping_status_final = case_when(
      is.na(nominee_name_clean_final) | nominee_name_clean_final == "" ~ "parse_failed",
      !is.na(gutsID_exact_final) & gutsID_exact_final != "" ~ "exact",
      TRUE ~ mapping_status
    ),

    gutsID_final = case_when(
      !is.na(gutsID_override_edit) & gutsID_override_edit != "" ~ gutsID_override_edit,
      mapping_status_final == "exact" ~ gutsID_exact_final,
      mapping_status == "exact" ~ gutsID_exact,
      TRUE ~ best_fuzzy_id
    ),

    keep_final = case_when(
      mapping_status == "exact" ~ TRUE,
      !is.na(keep_final_edit) ~ keep_final_edit,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )


# -------------------------
# Write FULL nomination-name audit
#   One row per nominee name across all sociometric columns, showing:
#   - whether it linked to a gutsID
#   - whether it was ever nominated by anyone
#   - how many total nominations it received
# -------------------------
full_nomination_audit_csv <- "S1_sociometric_nomination_name_audit.csv"

# Count nominations per sociometric column
soc_nomination_counts_by_col <- tibble(
  colname = soc_cols,

) %>%
```
